- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qemu-runner: Use this agent when you need to run a RISC-V ELF binary through Andes QEMU and get its output. Always use this agent instead of running QEMU directly, as it handles the semihosting fd 9 output capture quirk in Claude Code's sandbox.

Examples:

- assistant: *builds a test binary*
  assistant: "Let me use the qemu-runner agent to execute the binary and check the output"

- user: "Run this ELF at VLEN=512"
  assistant: "I'll use the qemu-runner agent to run it" (Tools: Bash, Read) (Tools: Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# andesim-demo test roadmap
2	
3	Each entry is one independent demo. One session builds ONE demo, then flips
4	its State and commits. States: `TODO`, `IN PROGRESS`, `DONE`, `BLOCKED`.
5	
6	Conventions (same as the existing demos):
7	
8	- Layout: `demo/<name>/main.c` + `demo/<name>/Makefile`; host-side checks go
9	  in `demo/<name>/check.sh` (the `memsize` precedent).
10	- Top-level `Makefile` gets `run-<name>` and the per-mode targets; `README.md`
11	  gets a short section describing what the demo proves.
12	- Pass signal: either the guest prints `<NAME>_OK` from inside the ROI, or
13	  `check.sh` asserts on the driver's output. Every demo must fail loudly.
14	- Demos run on every mode where the feature exists (some are hybrid-only or
15	  fast-only; each entry says which).
16	
17	Priority = file order. 1-3 are headline USER_GUIDE features with zero demo
18	coverage today.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## 1. hotloops
23	
24	State: TODO
25	Modes: hybrid (pc trigger); the detector itself runs fast.
26	
27	Measure a binary you cannot edit. `main.c` has one known hot loop (a
28	checksum over an array, >=10 iterations) and NO ROI markers. `check.sh`
29	runs `$(ANDESIM)/build/hotloops --min-iters 10 <elf>`, asserts the report
30	names the hot function, extracts the ready `measure:` line (a
31	`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair), and pastes it into
32	`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...`. Closed loop: the detector's
33	output feeds the measurement command with no human guessing.
34	
35	- Key files: `demo/hotloops/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
36	- Pass: check.sh sees the hot function in the hotloops report AND a
37	  `[andesim] N cycles` line from the hybrid run using the reported PCs.
38	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 4.3, docs/hotloops.md.
39	
40	## 2. verify
41	
42	State: DONE
43	Modes: hybrid only (marker trigger).
44	
45	Trust the figure. A state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP math under
46	RTZ, a strip-mined RVV loop, CSR writes staged before AND inside the ROI)
47	runs with `--verify`: andesim re-runs the ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
48	exit and compares the drained state field by field against the cycle
49	engine. Two builds from one source: `verify.elf` must PASS; the teeth are
50	`verify_taint.elf`, identical except one instruction sampling `mcycle`
51	into `t6` at the exit marker -- engine-divergent by design, so verify
52	must FAIL, name exactly `x31`, and exit non-zero. In the sweep the demo
53	is V-gated (`NEED_V`): the kernel uses RVV intrinsics.
54	
55	- Key files: `demo/verify/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
56	- Pass: check.sh asserts `[state-diff] PASS` + `[verify] PASS: vsim drain
57	  matches the QEMU oracle` on the clean build, and rc!=0 +
58	  `[state-diff] x31:` + `FAIL: 1 mismatch` on the taint build.
59	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.7.
60	
61	## 3. kanata
62	
63	State: TODO
64	Modes: hybrid only.
65	
66	See the pipeline of exactly the ROI. A small kernel runs with
67	`--kanata roi.kanata --objdump kernel.S` (the dump generated at build time
68	with `objdump -d`). Users open the file in Konata; check.sh proves it is
69	well-formed without a GUI.
70	
71	- Key files: `demo/kanata/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
72	- Pass: check.sh asserts the Kanata header line, that a known kernel
73	  mnemonic from the objdump is embedded, and the trace is non-trivial
74	  (more than a handful of retired instructions).
75	- Constraint to demo: marker mode needs exactly ONE exit marker in the ELF
76	  (more -> andesim errors and points at `--trigger pc`).
77	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.8.
78	
79	## 4. engines
80	
81	State: DONE
82	Modes: the whole suite, once per installed vsim engine.
83	
84	One suite, N cores - design-space switching, not a new demo dir. Every
85	demo's cycle/hybrid target already takes `ENGINE=<id>`, so the deliverable
86	is the sweep: `make check-all-engines` runs the aggregate `check` once per
87	vsim engine parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (restrict with
88	`SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a ..."`) and prints a per-engine OK/FAILED summary.
89	Demos are capability-gated per engine from the driver's own output: the
90	lm*/hvm* demos skip when the engine's resolved hybrid plan (`--dry-run`)
91	carries no ILM/DLM/HVM sidecar args (`ax46mpv_advanced` has none), and rvv
92	skips when the engine's `list engines` row shows no VLEN.
93	
94	- Key files: top `Makefile` (`check-all-engines`), `README.md`
95	- Pass: `make check-all-engines` exits 0. Teeth: a bogus engine in
96	  SWEEP_ENGINES makes the sweep report FAILED and exit nonzero.
97	- Deps: none.
98	
99	## 5. fp
100	
101	State: DONE
102	Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).
103	
104	Scalar FP state transport - fills the coverage gap next to `rvv` (which is
105	integer-V only). The QEMU phase sets a non-default rounding mode (`frm` =
106	RTZ) and raises a sticky `fflags` bit; the vsim ROI computes a
107	rounding-mode-sensitive result and checks: the result matches
108	expected-for-RTZ, and the pre-ROI sticky flag is still set. Proves
109	`fcsr` (+ `mstatus.FS`) crossed the handoff.
110	
111	- Key files: `demo/fp/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
112	- Pass: guest prints `FP_OK`.
113	- Deps: none.
114	
115	## 6. cache
116	
117	State: DONE
118	Modes: hybrid (marker), two variants of one source.
119	
120	Why timing-config transport matters. The same kernel is built twice from
121	one `main.c`: variant A keeps crt0's cache enable (transported
122	`mcache_ctl`), variant B writes `mcache_ctl = 0` before the ROI. check.sh
123	runs both hybrid measurements and asserts the uncached figure is much
124	larger. Doubles as a write-mask demo: the restore carries variant B's
125	disable only because the program itself wrote the CSR.
126	
127	- Key files: `demo/cache/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
128	- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(off) > 2 * cycles(on)` (calibrate the
129	  factor once real numbers exist).
130	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE section 6 ("Config that matters for
131	  timing rides along").
132	
133	## 7. roi_rules
134	
135	State: TODO
136	Modes: hybrid (marker + pc) vs cycle as the reference.
137	
138	Trigger semantics and measurement hygiene, executable. A `noinline` kernel
139	is called 3 times; both triggers are one-shot, so the measured window is

# andesim-demo test roadmap

Each entry is one independent demo. One session builds ONE demo, then flips
its State and commits. States: `TODO`, `IN PROGRESS`, `DONE`, `BLOCKED`.

Conventions (same as the existing demos):

- Layout: `demo/<name>/main.c` + `demo/<name>/Makefile`; host-side checks go
  in `demo/<name>/check.sh` (the `memsize` precedent).
- Top-level `Makefile` gets `run-<name>` and the per-mode targets; `README.md`
  gets a short section describing what the demo proves.
- Pass signal: either the guest prints `<NAME>_OK` from inside the ROI, or
  `check.sh` asserts on the driver's output. Every demo must fail loudly.
- Demos run on every mode where the feature exists (some are hybrid-only or
  fast-only; each entry says which).

Priority = file order. 1-3 are headline USER_GUIDE features with zero demo
coverage today.

---

## 1. hotloops

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (pc trigger); the detector itself runs fast.

Measure a binary you cannot edit. `main.c` has one known hot loop (a
checksum over an array, >=10 iterations) and NO ROI markers. `check.sh`
runs `$(ANDESIM)/build/hotloops --min-iters 10 <elf>`, asserts the report
names the hot function, extracts the ready `measure:` line (a
`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair), and pastes it into
`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...`. Closed loop: the detector's
output feeds the measurement command with no human guessing.

- Key files: `demo/hotloops/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh sees the hot function in the hotloops report AND a
  `[andesim] N cycles` line from the hybrid run using the reported PCs.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 4.3, docs/hotloops.md.

## 2. verify

State: DONE
Modes: hybrid only (marker trigger).

Trust the figure. A state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP math under
RTZ, a strip-mined RVV loop, CSR writes staged before AND inside the ROI)
runs with `--verify`: andesim re-runs the ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
exit and compares the drained state field by field against the cycle
engine. Two builds from one source: `verify.elf` must PASS; the teeth are
`verify_taint.elf`, identical except one instruction sampling `mcycle`
into `t6` at the exit marker -- engine-divergent by design, so verify
must FAIL, name exactly `x31`, and exit non-zero. In the sweep the demo
is V-gated (`NEED_V`): the kernel uses RVV intrinsics.

- Key files: `demo/verify/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `[state-diff] PASS` + `[verify] PASS: vsim drain
  matches the QEMU oracle` on the clean build, and rc!=0 +
  `[state-diff] x31:` + `FAIL: 1 mismatch` on the taint build.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.7.

## 3. kanata

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid only.

See the pipeline of exactly the ROI. A small kernel runs with
`--kanata roi.kanata --objdump kernel.S` (the dump generated at build time
with `objdump -d`). Users open the file in Konata; check.sh proves it is
well-formed without a GUI.

- Key files: `demo/kanata/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts the Kanata header line, that a known kernel
  mnemonic from the objdump is embedded, and the trace is non-trivial
  (more than a handful of retired instructions).
- Constraint to demo: marker mode needs exactly ONE exit marker in the ELF
  (more -> andesim errors and points at `--trigger pc`).
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.8.

## 4. engines

State: DONE
Modes: the whole suite, once per installed vsim engine.

One suite, N cores - design-space switching, not a new demo dir. Every
demo's cycle/hybrid target already takes `ENGINE=<id>`, so the deliverable
is the sweep: `make check-all-engines` runs the aggregate `check` once per
vsim engine parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (restrict with
`SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a ..."`) and prints a per-engine OK/FAILED summary.
Demos are capability-gated per engine from the driver's own output: the
lm*/hvm* demos skip when the engine's resolved hybrid plan (`--dry-run`)
carries no ILM/DLM/HVM sidecar args (`ax46mpv_advanced` has none), and rvv
skips when the engine's `list engines` row shows no VLEN.

- Key files: top `Makefile` (`check-all-engines`), `README.md`
- Pass: `make check-all-engines` exits 0. Teeth: a bogus engine in
  SWEEP_ENGINES makes the sweep report FAILED and exit nonzero.
- Deps: none.

## 5. fp

State: DONE
Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).

Scalar FP state transport - fills the coverage gap next to `rvv` (which is
integer-V only). The QEMU phase sets a non-default rounding mode (`frm` =
RTZ) and raises a sticky `fflags` bit; the vsim ROI computes a
rounding-mode-sensitive result and checks: the result matches
expected-for-RTZ, and the pre-ROI sticky flag is still set. Proves
`fcsr` (+ `mstatus.FS`) crossed the handoff.

- Key files: `demo/fp/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: guest prints `FP_OK`.
- Deps: none.

## 6. cache

State: DONE
Modes: hybrid (marker), two variants of one source.

Why timing-config transport matters. The same kernel is built twice from
one `main.c`: variant A keeps crt0's cache enable (transported
`mcache_ctl`), variant B writes `mcache_ctl = 0` before the ROI. check.sh
runs both hybrid measurements and asserts the uncached figure is much
larger. Doubles as a write-mask demo: the restore carries variant B's
disable only because the program itself wrote the CSR.

- Key files: `demo/cache/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(off) > 2 * cycles(on)` (calibrate the
  factor once real numbers exist).
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE section 6 ("Config that matters for
  timing rides along").

## 7. roi_rules

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (marker + pc) vs cycle as the reference.

Trigger semantics and measurement hygiene, executable. A `noinline` kernel
is called 3 times; both triggers are one-shot, so the measured window is
the FIRST call only. check.sh asserts the hybrid figure is far below the
cycle-mode total (which contains all 3 calls + boot). The source shows the
hygiene rule from USER_GUIDE 4.2: anchor the kernel through memory inside
the marker span.

- Key files: `demo/roi_rules/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(hybrid) < cycles(cycle) / 3`.
- Deps: none.

## 8. diagnose

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (driver features, no new guest code needed - reuse the hello ELF).

The debugging workflow as a script. check.sh exercises, in order:
`--dry-run` (asserts 2 resolved command lines), `--print-memmap` (asserts
the DRAM/V-scratch rows), `--log-level 1` (asserts the `[andesim] mmap`
line), `--log-file` (asserts timestamped, level-tagged lines land in the
file), and one forced leg failure that must leave a repro bundle
(`[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at ...` -> assert `manifest.txt`
exists there). Open point for the build session: pick the most reliable
quick failure (candidate: a `--pc-end` that never retires, with a short
timeout).

- Key files: `demo/diagnose/{Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: every assertion in check.sh.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.5, 5.6, 5.10, 8.

## 9. rv32

State: TODO
Modes: fast only (no rv32 cycle engine installed; hybrid rejects rv32 by design).

The rv32 runtime flavor and engine auto-select. Build hello against
`build/runtime/rv32` (`-march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d`), run `--mode fast` with
no `--engine`, and show the driver picked `qemu32` from the ELF width.

- Key files: `demo/rv32/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: hello output + exit code propagated; `--log-level 1` (or
  `--dry-run`) shows qemu32 was selected.
- Deps: needs an rv32-capable compiler (separate riscv32 gcc or multilib);
  the Makefile must skip with a clear message if the toolchain cannot do
  rv32.

## 10. gdb

State: TODO
Modes: fast first; cycle as a stretch goal.

Attach a debugger, scripted. fast: launch `--gdb` in the background, drive
`gdb-multiarch` in batch mode (`-ex 'target remote :1234'`, break at a
symbol, continue, print a variable, kill). cycle: needs `$ICEMAN` pointing
at an OpenOCD 0.12+ wrapper speaking remote_bitbang (the Andes-bundled
0.10 has a known bug against this DTM) - build only if the host has it.

- Key files: `demo/gdb/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: the gdb batch log shows the breakpoint hit and the expected
  variable value. check.sh skips (with a message) when gdb/OpenOCD are
  missing.
- Deps: none in-repo; host tools required. Build last.

## 11. priv

State: BLOCKED (engine not installed)
Modes: hybrid.

S/U-mode handoff: drop privilege before the ROI, prove the level and the
PMP mirror crossed. Requires the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired
with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66`; `./andesim list engines` currently shows only
the two M-mode-only engines. Unblock by installing that engine, then spec
the demo.

- Key files: `demo/priv/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: guest running in S-mode (or U-mode) inside the ROI prints `PRIV_OK`.
- Deps: ax66_makatau engine install.

# Shared configuration
-include Make.var

# Demos that run on every andesim mode (fast / cycle / hybrid).
SUBDIRS := demo/hello demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma \
           demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma demo/rvv demo/fp demo/cache \
           demo/verify demo/syscall demo/coremark demo/dhrystone demo/memsize

RUN_TARGETS := $(patsubst demo/%,run-%,$(SUBDIRS))

# RUN_TARGETS are deliberately NOT .PHONY: make never matches pattern
# rules (run-%) against .PHONY targets.
.PHONY: all run check check-all-engines clean $(SUBDIRS)

all: $(SUBDIRS)

$(SUBDIRS):
	$(MAKE) -C $@

run: $(RUN_TARGETS)

run-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/$* run

# Forward per-mode targets, e.g. `make hello-fast` -> demo/hello hello-fast.
hello-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello $@

lm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm $@

lm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_slave $@

lm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_dma $@

hvm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_slave $@

hvm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_dma $@

rvv-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/rvv $@

fp-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/fp $@

cache-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/cache $@

verify-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/verify $@

syscall-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/syscall $@

coremark-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/coremark $@

dhrystone-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/dhrystone $@

memsize-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/memsize $@

# Aggregate check: every demo that defines its own `check` runs it (real
# asserts); the rest are asserted to `run` cleanly (exit 0) across all modes.
# Continues past failures and reports a summary. Heavy -- coremark/dhrystone
# run their full cycle/hybrid legs. For one demo use `make check-<name>`.
check:
	@fail=""; \
	for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	  echo "########## $$dir ##########"; \
	  if $(MAKE) -C $$dir -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    $(MAKE) -C $$dir check || fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  elif $(MAKE) -C $$dir run; then \
	    echo "[PASS] $$dir: run exits 0 (no asserts)"; \
	  else \
	    echo "[FAIL] $$dir: run failed"; fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "===================================="; \
	if [ -z "$$fail" ]; then echo "ALL DEMOS OK"; \
	else echo "FAILED DEMOS:$$fail"; exit 1; fi

# ---- Engine sweep --------------------------------------------------------
# Demos that need hardware not every engine has. The sweep skips them on an
# engine whose resolved hybrid plan (--dry-run) carries no ILM/DLM/HVM
# sidecar args, or whose `list engines` row shows no VLEN.
NEED_LM  := demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma
NEED_HVM := demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma
NEED_V   := demo/rvv demo/verify

# Run the aggregate `check` once per installed vsim engine -- the engine set
# is parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (rv64 rows; the demos
# are rv64 builds). Restrict it with SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b". Fails if
# any engine fails any demo it is capable of.
check-all-engines:
	@engines="$(SWEEP_ENGINES)"; \
	if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
	  engines=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	             | awk '$$2 == "vsim" && $$4 == 64 { print $$1 }'); \
	fi; \
	if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
	  echo "no rv64 vsim engine installed (see: andesim list engines)"; exit 1; \
	fi; \
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello hello.elf >/dev/null; \
	summary=""; bad=""; \
	for eng in $$engines; do \
	  plan=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
	          --engine "$$eng" --dry-run demo/hello/hello.elf </dev/null 2>&1); \
	  vlen=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	          | awk -v e="$$eng" '$$1 == e { print $$5 }'); \
	  skips=""; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "ilm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_LM)"; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "hvm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_HVM)"; \
	  case "$$vlen" in ""|-|0) skips="$$skips $(NEED_V)";; esac; \
	  dirs=""; \
	  for d in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	    case " $$skips " in *" $$d "*) ;; *) dirs="$$dirs $$d";; esac; \
	  done; \
	  echo "#################### ENGINE $$eng ####################"; \
	  if [ -n "$$skips" ]; then echo "[SKIP] $$eng lacks the hardware for:$$skips"; fi; \
	  if $(MAKE) check ENGINE="$$eng" SUBDIRS="$$dirs"; then \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: OK (skipped:$${skips:- none})"; \
	  else \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: FAILED"; bad="$$bad $$eng"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "#################### ENGINE SWEEP ####################"; \
	printf "engines:$$summary\n"; \
	if [ -n "$$bad" ]; then echo "FAILED ENGINES:$$bad"; exit 1; fi

# Single demo: its own `check` if defined, else assert `run` exits 0.
check-%:
	@if $(MAKE) -C demo/$* -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* check; \
	else \
	  echo "demo/$*: no asserts -- running to assert exit 0"; \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* run; \
	fi

clean:
	@for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do $(MAKE) -C $$dir clean; done

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/rvv/       RVV-intrinsic kernel (8x8x8 GEMM) inside the ROI
demo/fp/        scalar FP state: frm steers a divide in the ROI, fflags stay sticky
demo/cache/     the mcache_ctl transport, priced: one kernel cached vs uncached
demo/verify/    --verify: the vsim drain vs the QEMU oracle, plus a taint build it must catch
demo/syscall/   stdio, host file io and exit code on every mode
demo/coremark/  EEMBC CoreMark; the ROI is the benchmark's own timed region
demo/dhrystone/ Dhrystone 2.2a; same recipe, two-pass compile kept
```

# ---- Shared configuration (can be overridden) ----

# Path to your andesim checkout, already built with scripts/build_all.sh.
ANDESIM ?= /home/nick/work/andesim

# Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `andesim doctor` reports).
XLEN ?= 64
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?= /local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d/bin/riscv$(XLEN)-unknown-elf-

COPILOT ?= 

# Cycle-accurate engine for --mode cycle / hybrid.
# See `andesim list engines` for what is available.
ENGINE ?= vsim:ax45mpv_premium

# Compiler optimization flag
OPT_LEVEL ?= -O2

# Extra flags for every andesim invocation, e.g. --log-level 1
ANDESIM_FLAGS ?=

# ---- Do not touch the followings ----

ANDESIM_BIN := $(ANDESIM)/andesim
RUNTIME := $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime

CC := $(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)gcc
OBJDUMP := $(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)objdump

# One ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid: link against the andesim runtime
# (UART stdio + SimControl exit, no semihosting). -B also puts the runtime's
# include/ on the search path, so <andesim/ROI.h> works.
CFLAGS := -march=rv$(XLEN)gc -mabi=lp64d $(OPT_LEVEL) \
          -B $(RUNTIME) -specs=andesim.specs

In the andesim project at /home/nick/work/andesim (a RISC-V hybrid simulator driver/runtime, NOT the andesim-demo repo), I need you to research (read-only, do NOT edit anything) why a guest program's `gettimeofday()` syscall fails specifically when run in `--mode cycle --engine vsim:ax66_makatau`, while the exact same ELF and syscall succeed fine on `--mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` and `--mode cycle --engine vsim:ax46mpv_advanced`, and also succeeds on `--mode fast` (plain QEMU) with any engine choice irrelevant.

Background: the guest runtime routes newlib syscalls (file io, gettimeofday, exit code) through an HTIF "magicmem" MMIO device at 0xe0080010, served host-side. In `--mode cycle`, the vsim RTL engine boots from reset with no QEMU pre-phase at all (unlike `--mode hybrid`, which runs a QEMU phase first then hands off to vsim). The observed guest-side symptom: `gettimeofday(&tv, NULL)` returns nonzero very early in `main()`, before any ROI/vector code runs — this is the FIRST syscall the guest makes at all in this program, right after boot.

ax66_makatau is notable because (per `andesim list engines`) it's the odd one out: XLEN=64, VLEN=128, ELEN=64 (the other two engines are VLEN=512, ELEN=32), and per this project's sibling repo's ROADMAP.md it's described as "the S/U-capable engine paired with QEMU -cpu andes-ax66" (the other two engines are M-mode only). So this may be a genuinely different RTL testbench/harness, not just a config knob.

What I need you to find and report back (concise, under 400 words):
1. Where is the HTIF/magicmem gettimeofday syscall handling implemented in the andesim driver (host-side) — is it engine-agnostic, or does it branch per engine/testbench?
2. Is there anything in the vsim engine registration/config (search for "ax66_makatau" across the andesim repo — its config files, engine list source, testbench glue) suggesting this engine's testbench wires up HTIF/magicmem differently, omits it, or has a known limitation (comments, TODOs, README notes)?
3. Is there a plausible reason tied to privilege mode (S/U-capable core) that HTIF magicmem polling/handshake could behave differently at boot for this engine — e.g. does the runtime's syscall stub or crt0 make an assumption (like running in M-mode) that would break under this engine's reset state?
4. Any existing test, doc, or comment (in andesim or its README/USER_GUIDE) that already acknowledges this engine has reduced/different capability versus the other two.

Do not attempt to fix anything or run any simulations — this is pure investigation. Report file:line citations for every claim. If you cannot find a definitive root cause, say so plainly and report your best-supported hypothesis plus what would need to be checked (e.g., RTL testbench source, which may live outside this repo) to confirm it.

No TODO/comment mentions magicmem/HTIF directly.

**3. Best-supported root-cause hypothesis (privilege-adjacent, but via config not boot state).**
`crt0.S`/`handler.c` use only M-mode CSRs with no privilege probe, but since `main()` demonstrably runs, the hart is in M-mode as expected on all three engines — ruling out "wrong boot privilege." Two independently-documented problems then apply: `driver/memmap.hpp:22-24` states the L2C window is "intentionally absent... every current engine is built `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`," and `docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md:233-242` (M2) says a store to an absent L2C device "does not get ignored — it faults"; separately, M5 (`hybrid_state_transport_problems.md:277-289`) requires **sub-8-byte** access to these registers ("never `sd`/`ld`"), which `flush_dcache()` violates regardless. Either would derail `gettimeofday` before the real HTIF trigger write executes — on ax66_makatau only.

**4. No existing acknowledgment found.** Registration validation (`registration_report.md:47-58`) was only `--mode hybrid`; no `--mode cycle` cold-boot test for this engine exists in `tests/engines/`. `driver/memmap.hpp`'s "every engine has zero L2C" line wasn't revisited by the ax66 registration commit.

**To confirm:** inspect the external vsim repo's `platform/memory_map.h` / bus-fault behavior at `0xe0500000` for ax66_makatau, and whether `sim_control.hpp`'s HTIF table branches per engine.</result>

1	// The hybrid guest memory map: which regions a workload may touch in
2	// `run --mode hybrid`, composed from the same sources the run itself trusts.
3	//
4	// Only hybrid-SUPPORTED regions appear (PM rule): regions modeled by BOTH
5	// engines whose content or device behavior the handoff actually provides.
6	// QEMU-only devices (MROM/PLIC/PLMT/virtio/...), vsim-reserved holes (PLDM),
7	// and unverified-parity devices (UART1/SMU) are deliberately absent.
8	//
9	// Sources, in provenance order:
10	//   - DRAM + V-scratch: the driver's own window math (--mem-size; the
11	//     reserved HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES page above program RAM, L26).
12	//   - ILM/DLM/HVM bases: the engine's `--print-qemu-config` text -- the same
13	//     staged qemu.cfg the QEMU fast leg boots with, so the printed bases are
14	//     exactly the run's effective geometry.
15	//   - ILM/DLM/HVM sizes + row presence: the engine descriptor's backdoor-gated
16	//     ilm/dlm/hvm_size (0 = content cannot cross the handoff -> row omitted).
17	//   - SimControl/HTIF + UART2: fixed AE350 platform constants, identical in
18	//     QEMU (hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c memmap table) and vsim (platform
19	//     memory_map.h); drift is guarded by tests/andes_sim/
20	//     test_andes_sim_print_memmap.sh, which cross-checks the engine's own
21	//     `--print-memmap` dump.
22	//   - L2C register window (0xe0500000): intentionally absent until an engine
23	//     ships with an L2C -- `--describe` carries no L2C capability today, and
24	//     every current engine is built _NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0.

26	#define ANDESIM_MEMMAP_HPP
27	
28	#include <cstdint>

30	#include <string>
31	#include <vector>
32

39	  uint64_t base = 0;      // guest physical, first byte

content.content:
4. Drain reads CEN=0; restore writes CEN=0 into vsim.
5. The ROI runs with L2 OFF: cycle count several times too big, and
   no error is printed anywhere.

**Status: SOLVED for the register that matters.** QEMU seeds the
Control register's spec reset (CEN=1) at machine init
(`hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c`, commit 86d433001e); proven by
`test_plugin_l2c_reset_default.sh` (a guest that never writes 0x0008
still drains CEN=1). Safe to hardcode because CEN=1 is an IP-spec
constant, not an engine choice -- and once the defaults agree, C1's
"who wrote it" trap is harmless for this register: both readings give
the same, correct value. Other L2C registers are NOT seeded -- see M6.

## M2. Restoring into an absent device FAULTS

**What happens.** MMIO restore is a store instruction executed by the
halted hart (through the Program Buffer). If this engine was built
WITHOUT the device, there is nothing at that address: the store is a
bus error, the Program Buffer faults, and the whole resume aborts.
Unlike a CSR (C2), there is no "tolerant" mode for memory.

**Example.** Every current engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`.
A `sw` to 0xE0500008 on them does not get ignored -- it faults.

**Status: SOLVED (*).** Hard presence gate: `Simulator::l2c_present()`
reads the engine's own build config (`_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`) and
`ResumeDriver::restore_l2c` / `StateDrain::drain_l2c` issue nothing
when absent (vsim `resume_driver.hpp`/`state_drain.hpp`/
`simulator.hpp`). Unit-tested both ways (flag clear / device absent).

## M3. Some device registers are buttons, not storage

**What happens.** Writing certain MMIO registers triggers an action or
destroys state, so "write the drained value back" is wrong for them.

**Examples.** L2C CCTL Command register: writing 0x12 STARTS a full L2
flush -- restoring it would run a cache flush inside the measured
window. W1C error bits: writing 1 CLEARS them. The Configuration
register is read-only anyway.

**Status: SOLVED (*).** The plugin captures the WHOLE 0x0000..0x0527
window into the file; `restore_l2c` writes back only the whitelist --
Control (0x0008), HPM Control (0x0010), Way Allocation Masks
(0x0300..) -- never CCTL/W1C/RO registers (`resume_driver.hpp`; offsets
defined in `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`). (Mirror: C5.)

## M4. Some device status changes by itself

**What happens.** Status bits driven by the device, not the program,
cannot match between a functional model and a cycle model.

**Example.** L2C `INITSTATUS[14]`: a real L2C drives it while its TAG
RAMs initialize; QEMU's RAM stub never changes it.

**Status: SOLVED.** `state_diff.cpp` compares `l2c.ctrl` with bit 14
masked out; unit-tested. (Mirror: C4.)

## M5. The device dictates the access width

**What happens.** Device buses have rules; breaking them is
UNPREDICTABLE per the spec.

**Example.** DS220 11.8.3: L2C registers must be accessed with single
transfers SMALLER than 8 bytes. So the transport must use `sw`/`lwu`
(32-bit), never `sd`/`ld` (64-bit).

**Status: SOLVED (*).** `encode_sw`/`encode_lwu` word accesses in the
Program Buffer (vsim `src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp`), `lwu`
(zero-extend) so a 32-bit read does not sign-pollute the 64-bit file
slot. Golden-hex unit tests from `riscv64-elf-as`. (Mirror: C6.)

## M6. The stub lies to programs that READ it

**What happens.** Boot code may read device config and branch on it.
QEMU's RAM stub returns whatever is in RAM (mostly zeros), not what the
real device would report -- and the wrong branch has already run by the

content.text:
All 3 vsim engines tested. Result: **2 pass, 1 fails.**

| Engine | Result |
|---|---|
| `vsim:ax45mpv_premium` | PASS |
| `vsim:ax46mpv_advanced` | PASS (lm/hvm demos skipped - no local memory hardware, expected) |
| `vsim:ax66_makatau` | **FAIL** on `demo/syscall` |

**Root cause (verified by reading the actual source, not just the agent's word):**

The guest runtime's syscall shim (`andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c:72-103`) does this before every single HTIF syscall: check CSR `mmsc_cfg` bit 46 ("L2 cache present" flag). If set, it writes/polls L2-cache-control registers at `0xe0500008/40/80` using 64-bit `ld`/`sd`.

- `ax66_makatau` is the only one of the 3 engines whose chip config reports that bit as **1** (confirmed in `tests/engines/ax66_makatau-5937b880/rtl_params.json`: `PL2C_SUPPORT: 1`). The other two engines don't have that capability bit at all.
- But `andesim/driver/memmap.hpp:22-24` and `docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md` (problem M2) both say plainly: **no engine actually has this L2 hardware built** (`_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` on all of them, ax66_makatau included). So this engine's config says "I have L2" while its hardware says "I don't."
- Result: on `ax66_makatau`, the guest trusts the CSR flag, touches a register address that isn't really there, and that appears to break the syscall protocol on the very first syscall the guest makes (`gettimeofday`, right after boot) - matching the exact failure we saw.
- Separate, smaller bug in the same code: the spec (DS220 11.8.3, also cited in that same doc, problem M5) says L2 registers must be accessed in <8-byte chunks (`sw`/`lwu`), but this code uses 64-bit `ld`/`sd` - wrong either way.

This bug lives in the `andesim` repo (`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`), not in `andesim-demo` - your demo suite and its `check-all-engines` tooling did exactly their job by catching it.

`make check-all-engines` (in andesim-demo) sweeps all 3 vsim engines
(`ax45mpv_premium`, `ax46mpv_advanced`, `ax66_makatau`) and found
`vsim:ax66_makatau` fails `demo/syscall` in `--mode cycle`: the guest's
first-ever syscall, `gettimeofday()`, fails right after boot
(`SYSCALL_STAGE_BAD gettimeofday`, exit 2). The other two engines and
`--mode fast` pass fine.

Root cause, verified by reading source directly (2026-07-13):
- `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c:72-103` (`flush_dcache()`, called by
  every `htif_syscall()`) checks CSR `mmsc_cfg` bit 46 ("L2 present").
  If set, it touches L2C control registers at `0xe0500008/40/80` with
  64-bit `ld`/`sd`.
- `ax66_makatau` is the only one of the 3 engines whose RTL decoder
  reports that bit as 1 (`tests/engines/ax66_makatau-5937b880/rtl_params.json`:
  `PL2C_SUPPORT: 1`; the other two engines have no such param at all).
- But `andesim/driver/memmap.hpp:22-24` and
  `andesim/docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md` problem M2 both say
  NO current engine actually has the L2C hardware built
  (`_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` everywhere, ax66_makatau included). So this
  engine's capability CSR says "L2 present" while the hardware disagrees.
- Guest trusts the CSR bit, touches a register that isn't really there
  -> breaks the HTIF syscall protocol on the very first syscall call.
- Second, independent bug in the same function: same doc's problem M5
  says L2C registers need <8-byte access (`sw`/`lwu`), but the code uses
  64-bit `ld`/`sd` regardless.

**Why this matters:** the bug lives in `/home/nick/work/andesim`
(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`), a sibling repo to `andesim-demo` (this
project) - not something to fix inside andesim-demo. `andesim-demo`'s
own `check-all-engines` tooling (ROADMAP item 4, already DONE) is
working exactly as designed by catching this.

**How to apply:** if asked again to test/sweep engines, expect this
exact failure on `ax66_makatau` until the andesim repo fixes
`flush_dcache()` (options as of this writing: gate the L2 flush on
actual `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB`, not just the `mmsc_cfg` capability bit;
and/or fix the access width to `sw`/`lwu`). User was asked whether to
fix it (in andesim, cross-repo) or investigate whether `PL2C_SUPPORT=1`
is itself a vsim RTL misconfiguration (`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`)
and did not respond yet - do not assume which direction they want;
ask again if this resurfaces.

name: ax66-makatau-syscall-bug
description: vsim:ax66_makatau engine fails demo/syscall in --mode cycle due to a real bug in the andesim repo (not andesim-demo)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

---

`make check-all-engines` (in andesim-demo) sweeps all 3 vsim engines
(`ax45mpv_premium`, `ax46mpv_advanced`, `ax66_makatau`) and found
`vsim:ax66_makatau` fails `demo/syscall` in `--mode cycle`: the guest's
first-ever syscall, `gettimeofday()`, fails right after boot
(`SYSCALL_STAGE_BAD gettimeofday`, exit 2). The other two engines and
`--mode fast` pass fine.

Root cause, verified by reading source directly (2026-07-13):
- `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c:72-103` (`flush_dcache()`, called by
  every `htif_syscall()`) checks CSR `mmsc_cfg` bit 46 ("L2 present").
  If set, it touches L2C control registers at `0xe0500008/40/80` with
  64-bit `ld`/`sd`.
- `ax66_makatau` is the only one of the 3 engines whose RTL decoder
  reports that bit as 1 (`tests/engines/ax66_makatau-5937b880/rtl_params.json`:
  `PL2C_SUPPORT: 1`; the other two engines have no such param at all).
- But `andesim/driver/memmap.hpp:22-24` and
  `andesim/docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md` problem M2 both say
  NO current engine actually has the L2C hardware built
  (`_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` everywhere, ax66_makatau included). So this
  engine's capability CSR says "L2 present" while the hardware disagrees.
- Guest trusts the CSR bit, touches a register that isn't really there
  -> breaks the HTIF syscall protocol on the very first syscall call.
- Second, independent bug in the same function: same doc's problem M5
  says L2C registers need <8-byte access (`sw`/`lwu`), but the code uses
  64-bit `ld`/`sd` regardless.

**Why this matters:** the bug lives in `/home/nick/work/andesim`
(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`), a sibling repo to `andesim-demo` (this
project) - not something to fix inside andesim-demo. `andesim-demo`'s
own `check-all-engines` tooling (ROADMAP item 4, already DONE) is
working exactly as designed by catching this.

**How to apply:** if asked again to test/sweep engines, expect this
exact failure on `ax66_makatau` until the andesim repo fixes
`flush_dcache()` (options as of this writing: gate the L2 flush on
actual `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB`, not just the `mmsc_cfg` capability bit;
and/or fix the access width to `sw`/`lwu`). User was asked whether to
fix it (in andesim, cross-repo) or investigate whether `PL2C_SUPPORT=1`
is itself a vsim RTL misconfiguration (`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`)
and did not respond yet - do not assume which direction they want;
ask again if this resurfaces.

**CONFIRMED: not an RTL bug, it's a software bug (2026-07-13 follow-up).**
Checked `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/external/ax66/andes_ip/mk_core/ucore/csr/hdl/mk_csr.v`
directly. Line 433: `localparam PL2C_SUPPORT = 1; //*always support PL2C
for AX66 even if SIZE = 0KB` - this is an explicit, intentional vendor
design choice, not an oversight. Every other cache support flag in this
file IS size-gated (e.g. `ICACHE_SUPPORT = (ICACHE_SIZE_KB > 0) ? 1 :
0`); PL2C_SUPPORT is the one deliberate exception. The actually-correct,
size-aware CSR is `MPL2CM_CFG` (0xfdf): its `dsz`/`dway` fields are
properly gated on `PL2C_SIZE_KB == 0` (line 14818-14824, "no pl2
cache"). `PL2C_SIZE_KB` itself is a real configurable `parameter`
(line 280) currently 0 for this build - consistent with andesim's
`_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` claim.

So: `mmsc_cfg`'s coarse PL2C "support" bit is genuinely, deliberately 1
on ax66_makatau regardless of size; the RTL exposes the real answer
("is there actually a cache") through a different CSR
(`MPL2CM_CFG`/dsz-dway), which the andesim guest code never reads. The
bug is 100% in `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`'s `flush_dcache()`:
it must not treat the coarse support bit as "safe to touch L2C MMIO",
either checking `MPL2CM_CFG`'s size fields first, or another safe
gate.

**Why this matters:** the bug lives in `/home/nick/work/andesim`
(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`), a sibling repo to `andesim-demo` (this
project) - not something to fix inside andesim-demo. `andesim-demo`'s
own `check-all-engines` tooling (ROADMAP item 4, already DONE) is
working exactly as designed by catching this.

**How to apply:** if asked again to test/sweep engines, expect this
exact failure on `ax66_makatau` until `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`
is fixed to check `MPL2CM_CFG` size fields (not just `mmsc_cfg`'s PL2C
bit) before touching L2C MMIO, and/or fixes the `ld`/`sd` access width
to `sw`/`lwu` per spec. Root cause is now fully resolved/confirmed -
no need to re-investigate the RTL side again. User has not yet said
whether to apply the fix (cross-repo, in andesim) - ask before editing
that repo.

content.text:
**No — it's not a real RTL misconfiguration. The RTL deliberately sets it that way, on purpose.**

Found it directly in the vsim RTL source: `vsim_andesim/external/ax66/andes_ip/mk_core/ucore/csr/hdl/mk_csr.v:433`

```verilog
localparam PL2C_SUPPORT = 1; //*always support PL2C for AX66 even if SIZE = 0KB
```

That comment is the vendor's own words. Compare to every other cache flag in the same file, which correctly turns off when size is 0:
```verilog
localparam ICACHE_SUPPORT = (ICACHE_SIZE_KB > 0) ? 1 : 0;
localparam DCACHE_SUPPORT = (DCACHE_SIZE_KB > 0) ? 1 : 0;
```
`PL2C_SUPPORT` is the one deliberate exception - hardcoded to 1 no matter what.

The RTL *does* have a correct, size-aware answer - it's just in a different CSR. `PL2C_SIZE_KB` (line 280) is a real, configurable parameter, set to 0 for this build. And `MPL2CM_CFG` (CSR 0xfdf), a separate register, correctly reports "no cache" when size is 0 (`mk_csr.v:14818-14824`: `dsz`/`dway` fields go to 0 exactly when `PL2C_SIZE_KB == 0`).

So: `mmsc_cfg`'s PL2C bit means "this core architecturally knows about PL2C," not "this core has a PL2C cache right now." The guest code (`andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) only checks the first one. That's the bug - confirmed 100% in the `andesim` repo's software, not in the vsim RTL. I updated the saved finding to reflect this; no more ambiguity to chase here.

Since the RTL side is closed out, do you want me to fix `vplat_syscalls.c` now (in the `andesim` repo), or leave it for later?

- **Sign B** (inside): "Garage size: 0." This sign correctly says there is no garage.

Why two signs that disagree? The chip maker did this **on purpose**. They even left a note: "always say yes to Sign A, even if size is 0." So Sign A is not a mistake by the chip maker.

Now, our startup program (the code that runs first) only reads **Sign A**. It sees "YES, garage exists" and tries to park a car there. But there is no garage. So it crashes.

**The real problem:** the program should have read **Sign B** (the real size = 0), not Sign A. This program is in a different project folder (`andesim`, not `andesim-demo`).

So:
- Chip design = correct, working as intended.
- Program that starts the chip = has a bug (reads the wrong sign).

We could, but it would only hide the problem, not fix it.

**Yes, technically possible:** Our Makefile already does this trick for OTHER things. It runs the chip, asks "what do you have?" (`--dry-run`, `list engines`), and skips tests that don't apply — for example, it skips memory tests on chips that don't have that memory. We could add a similar rule: "if chip = ax66_makatau, skip the gettimeofday test."

**But this case is different, and skipping is the wrong move here:**

1. Those other skips are for hardware that is **really not there** (fair to skip — nothing is broken, the feature just doesn't exist on that chip).
2. This case is a **bug** (the program reads the wrong sign), not missing hardware. If we skip it, we only stop OUR TEST from noticing. The real chip still crashes for any real program that hits this path. We'd just be closing our eyes to it.

**There's also a stronger reason not to "ask which chip" — it's true for the actual fix, not just our test:**

The buggy program (`vplat_syscalls.c`) was written with a strict rule: NEVER ask "which chip am I on." I read this rule directly in the file's own comment. Why such a strict rule? Because in "hybrid" mode, a program can start running on one chip (QEMU) and then get moved to a DIFFERENT chip (vsim) partway through — like swapping horses mid-race. If the program asked "which chip am I on" only once, near the start, that answer becomes wrong the moment it gets swapped. So the file's rule is: never check "which chip", always just read the correct sign, whichever chip you happen to be on.

**So the best fix is:** teach the program to always read Sign B (the real, always-true answer), instead of Sign A (the sign that can lie on this one chip). This fixes ax66_makatau, and it automatically protects against any FUTURE chip with the same kind of lie — without us keeping a list of "which chips are broken" to remember and update.

My recommendation: fix the program to read Sign B. Skipping in our test only hides the bug from ourselves.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
* Always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something changed.

## Repository Overview

Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a two-phase handoff: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta; there is no QEMU2 leg (the handback was removed).

One Git submodule:
- `include/` - the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): the `hybrid_state_v1` wire
  contract under `include/hybrid/`, pinned by andesim AND by the external vsim, so
  there is one source of truth.

QEMU and vsim are NOT submodules -- both are prebuilt external binaries:
- QEMU: point `QEMU_BIN_DIR` (config.env) at your `qemu-system-*` build dir.
- vsim: point `VSIM_BIN_DIR` (config.env) at your external vsim `build/` dir (the
  `sim_*` binaries). The vsim sources -- including the vsim-side hybrid
  orchestration (`src/hybrid/*.hpp`), `CMakeLists.txt`, and `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake`
  referenced throughout this doc -- live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo and are
  built there (its own `build_vsim.sh`), no longer nested under `verilator/` here.

## Build Commands

**Primary path (`./andesim`)** -- the end-user driver (C++, self-builds on
first use), the only driver, used in all user-facing docs.

```sh
bash scripts/build_all.sh        # builds qemu, vsim, plugin, fixtures
bash scripts/test_all.sh         # unit + contract + e2e suite
./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc] [--engine ID] <elf>
./andesim list <models|engines>
```

**Developer escape hatch** -- the underlying scripts. Use these when
working on the build system, the harness, or a single leg in isolation:

```sh
# Build everything (locate external qemu -> vsim -> plugin)
source ./setup.sh

# QEMU and vsim are NOT built here -- both are prebuilt external binaries. Point
# config.env's QEMU_BIN_DIR at your qemu-system-* build dir and VSIM_BIN_DIR at
# your external vsim build/ dir (see config.env.example); setup.sh validates both
# and exports VSIM_QEMU / VSIM_BIN_DIR.

# Build individual components (vsim is built in its own external checkout)
make -C qemu_plugin                        # TCG plugins (out-of-tree; vendored qemu-plugin.h, no QEMU source needed)

# Build RISC-V ELF test fixtures
make -C tests/fixtures              # all fixtures
make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_regs.elf  # single fixture

# Clean (vsim is external; not cleaned here)
source ./setup.sh clean [plugin|all]
```

**Outputs:**
- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so` (+ `libhotloops.so`)
- the vsim `sim_*` binaries are produced in the external vsim checkout under
  `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` (e.g. `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium`).

QEMU and vsim are integrated as prebuilt external binaries, not built here:
`$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64` and `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_*` (set both in
`config.env`). The vsim repo's own `build_vsim.sh` is Docker-based (podman): it
builds an image from its `Dockerfile` (target `env`), runs `./build.sh` inside,
and pins the shared ABI as a nested submodule at `external/andesim_abi`.

## Running Tests

```sh
# All e2e tests in parallel (auto-detects job count from nproc + /dev/shm headroom)
bash scripts/run_e2e.sh

# Run with specific options
JOBS=4 MODE=marker bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # 4-way parallel, marker-mode only
JOBS=1 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                  # sequential (debug)
FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh           # regex filter on fixture name
LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs bash scripts/run_e2e.sh    # custom log directory

# Unit tests (inside vsim build container)
# The container build runs: cmake --build build -j
# To run ctest directly after build:
#   podman run ... ./build.sh && podman exec ... ctest --test-dir build -L hybrid-e2e
```

**Important:** on a high-core-count machine (128+ cores) `default_jobs()` computes `min(nproc, /dev/shm_free/256MB)` which can reach 128+. Running that many vsim Verilator processes simultaneously saturates CPU and causes timeouts. Use `JOBS=8` (or lower) as a practical cap: `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.

`scripts/run_e2e.sh` exits 0 only when all tests pass. Logs go to a `mktemp` directory under `/tmp`; path is printed at the start of each run. Each test's full output lands in `$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log`.

**Manual driver tests**: `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh` cover the C++ driver's feature contracts. They run manually during driver development, not wired into `scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Each script is self-contained (sources `setup.sh` artifacts, runs one subcommand, asserts on stdout). The same convention applies to `tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh` (QEMU-plugin-only smoke tests).

## Architecture

### Two-Phase Handoff

```
QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
```

206 CLAUDE.md
---

1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On the marker trigger (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands, one write per register. Every CSR write -- the base M-mode scalars, the Andes V5 block, and the M-ext block -- also goes through Abstract Commands only, one write per CSR; there is no batched Program-Buffer sweep anywhere in the register/CSR transport, in either direction (a WARL/read-only CSR faulting mid-batch can't be tolerated the way the abstract path's per-CSR cmderr-clear can). `StateDrain` mirrors this: one abstract read per GPR/FPR/CSR. This is the MMIO analog of the `mcache_ctl` (L1-enable) transport, and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. **Restore is HARD-gated on the engine having an L2C** (`Simulator::l2c_present()` from `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`): a store to an absent L2C region faults the Program Buffer, unlike a tolerant CSR write. Every current engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`, so the block is transported forward-looking and the restore/drain no-op today. QEMU seeds the L2C Control Register's reset value (`CEN=1`, DS220 11.8.7) at machine init (`andes_ae350.c`), so a guest that relies on the default is not drained as `CEN=0`.

### V-State Transport

V data registers (v0..v31) move through a scratch region in the shared mmap.
L26: that region is the mmap's TOP page, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) =
ram_base + ram_size - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`, NOT a fixed address. The driver
maps one page more than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes`), so the
scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size`, just above the program's RAM, where no
program layout can collide with it (`cmd_run` also rejects an ELF whose static
image would reach into it). `ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain` take the GPA as a
required-when-V argument (the simulator passes `v_scratch_gpa()`); a V handoff
with it unset throws. vsim drives the transfer via the Debug Module **Program
Buffer** while the hart is halted, so benchmark binaries issue no transport code:
- `stage_v_to_scratch` copies `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` into the scratch region
  before resume; `ResumeDriver` then sweeps `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch into the
  regfile (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=true).
- At drain, `StateDrain` sweeps `vse8.v v0..v31` from the regfile back to scratch
  (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=false); `read_v_from_scratch` lifts the bytes into
  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` (the drained handoff file; there is no QEMU2 ship step).

Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m8 (vl=8*vlenb), which also forces vstart=0;
with LMUL=8 one `vle8.v`/`vse8.v` moves a group of 8 registers, so all 32 move in
4 grouped ops in a single Program-Buffer execution. The scratch is packed at the
RUNTIME vlenb stride (`stage_v_to_scratch` drops the wire-format
`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` padding so each 8-register group is contiguous).

V scalar CSR transport (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr):
- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS
- **Tier B** (Program Buffer): vtype + vl via `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` (direct CSR write to vtype sets vill; vl is read-only; only `vsetvl` restores both atomically)

Restore order in `ResumeDriver::resume()` when `HYBRID_FLAG_V` is set:
1. `mstatus.VS` (enables V in the hart)
2. V-data reload sweep: `vsetvl` e8/m8 then `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch in the
   Program Buffer. Runs BEFORE the architectural V-CSR restore (whose `vsetvl`
   overwrites the sweep's vtype/vl/vstart) and uses x5/x6/x7 as scratch.
3. `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in Program Buffer (stages `vl` in x5, `vtype` in x6 via abstract GPR writes first)
4. `vstart` (AFTER vsetvl: vsetvl resets vstart to 0)
5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)

`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` issues the matching `vse8.v` dump sweep
LAST, after every architectural read (GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret), so the
sweep's clobbers and any counter increments cannot corrupt the drained state.

### Test Fixtures

All fixtures run on the unified `tests/e2e.sh` harness, which
sets up an `/dev/shm`-backed shared mmap (128 MB) so memory survives
the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. Three fixture families:

| Family   | Examples                                                    | Notes |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
| asm      | `handoff_roundtrip`, `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_shared_mem` | no C runtime; don't strictly need shared mmap but use it anyway (~20 ms cost is negligible). |
| C-level  | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`   | hybrid round-trip tests, linked through the vplat runtime (below). Shared mmap is REQUIRED -- vsim resumes on QEMU1's memory, so the stack/heap and `main()`'s frame must survive the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. |
| vplat    | `vplat_hello`, `vplat_exit41`, `vplat_file`                 | smoke tests for the runtime's own features (exit code, file io). The runtime is engine-portable, shipped as `build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a` (sources in `runtime/`; build with `make -C runtime` or `scripts/build_all.sh runtime`): UART stdio + SimControl exit + HTIF file io, NO semihosting -- the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. Users link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. See docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 4; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`. |

The shared mmap is created with `mktemp -p /dev/shm` + `truncate`,
then QEMU is launched with `-object memory-backend-file`.

Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`; the shared runtime sources live at the repo root in `runtime/`. ALL C fixtures (rt_c_* and vplat_*) link through the shipped vplat runtime with the user command (`-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`); nothing in-tree links `-lgloss_vh` or uses semihosting syscalls anymore (asm fixtures still carry a semihosting exit fallback from `semihost_exit.inc`). V-using fixtures require `-march=rv64gcv`. Syscalls bottom out in MMIO devices both engines model (UART2 `0xf0300000`, SimControl/HTIF `0xe0080000` -- QEMU side is inline in `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c`), so a `printf` inside the ROI works on every engine (it just adds the real UART cycles to the figure); the old "Phase-2 no-syscall rule" survives only as a measurement-hygiene convention in cycle-measuring fixtures, and as a hard rule for user binaries that still link a semihosting libgloss.
