Live only when `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` is set (the plugin sets it when QEMU's gdbstub advertised at least one Andes CSR). All restores are tolerant (a core lacking the CSR no-ops the write); the block round-trips through the trap-free ROI and is `--verify`-compared, except `msp_bound`/`msp_base` (HW stack-protection bounds) and `milmb`/`mdlmb` (ILM/DLM base+enable) which are engine-reset-divergent -- QEMU resets `msp_bound`/`msp_base` to all-ones (a vsim core without HW stack protection drains 0), and drains the `milmb`/`mdlmb` enable bit clear while the vsim RTL drains it set -- so they are verify-excluded like `mip`.

**v5 L2C block**: `struct hybrid_l2c` carries the **L2 cache controller's MMIO register window** (`reg[]` = offsets 0x0000..0x0527, DS220 11.8.5 Table 112). Unlike every other block this is DEVICE MMIO, not a CSR: the plugin drains the whole window with `qemu_plugin_read_memory_hwaddr` (physical address `l2c_base`, default 0xE0500000), and `ResumeDriver::restore_l2c` writes back ONLY the writable boot-static config registers -- Control (0x0008: `CEN` enable + prefetch + ECC + RAM timing), HPM Control (0x0010), Way Allocation Masks (0x0300..0x0328) -- via Program-Buffer word stores (`sw`, per DS220 11.8.3's <8-byte access rule). The read-only Configuration Register, the side-effecting CCTL command registers (writing one re-issues an L2 cache op), and the W1C error registers are captured but never restored. `StateDrain::drain_l2c` re-reads the config registers (`lwu`) for `--verify` (`state_diff` compares `l2c.ctrl` with the RO INITSTATUS[14] bit masked). This is the MMIO analog of the `mcache_ctl` (L1-enable) transport, and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. **Restore is HARD-gated on the engine having an L2C** (`Simulator::l2c_present()` from `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`): a store to an absent L2C region faults the Program Buffer, unlike a tolerant CSR write. Every current engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`, so the block is transported forward-looking and the restore/drain no-op today. QEMU seeds the L2C Control Register's reset value (`CEN=1`, DS220 11.8.7) at machine init (`andes_ae350.c`), so a guest that relies on the default is not drained as `CEN=0`.

**v6 write-mask**: `write_mask[2]` (one bit per mask-governed config CSR, slot map + decode helpers in `include/hybrid/write_mask.h`, live under `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) records **which CSRs the guest actually WROTE** during the QEMU phase. The plugin decodes CSR-write instructions at translation time (`csrrw`/`csrrwi` always write; `csrrs/c` only when rs1!=x0; `csrrsi/ci` only when uimm!=0) and registers an exec callback only on instructions that write a mask-governed CSR -- steady-state code carries zero instrumentation, so the fast leg is unaffected. Consumers (`ResumeDriver` restore, `state_diff` verify) skip any governed CSR whose bit is clear: an untouched CSR's drained value is only QEMU's reset default, which can legitimately differ from the engine's RTL reset value (`msp_bound` all-ones vs 0, `milmb.IEN` 0 vs 1), so skipping keeps the engine at ITS OWN reset value -- what real silicon of that engine would hold -- and makes producer/engine reset divergence harmless by construction for every current and future engine, with no per-engine data in QEMU. Governed set: the v3 Andes scalars + PMA, the v4 M-ext block, `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`. Never governed: GPRs/FPRs/V, mstatus, dpc/dcsr, counters, fcsr, the trap-writable CSRs (mepc/mcause/mtval/mip/mie -- hardware writes them without a CSR insn), mtvec/mscratch, and PMP (the S/U mirror is a correctness requirement). `ucode` is transport-always (DSP ops set its sticky OV flag without a CSR insn). Flag clear (pre-v6 file) -> consumers fall back to restore/compare-everything.

**Memory-content sidecars (NOT in `hybrid_state_v1`)**: ILM/DLM and HVM content travels OUTSIDE the state struct, as raw binary sidecar files next to each state file. The plugin (args `ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size` in bytes; bases default `0xA0000000`/`0xA0200000`/`0x90000000`) drains `<state>.ilm/.dlm/.hvm` through the slave-port/subordinate apertures; the vsim leg backdoor-loads them (`--ilm/--dlm/--hvm` -- zero-sim-cycle Verilator hierarchical-reference pokes into the RTL SRAMs, NOT the DM Program Buffer); the exit drain dumps the read-duals next to the handoff-out state. Armed by the engine's `--describe` sizes (`ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size`, bytes; 0 = no memory or wrapper lacks the set_*/get_* backdoor pair -- capability-gated so a config-has-it/wrapper-can't engine arms nothing). These QEMU memories are per-CPU overlays (LM) or standalone RAM (HVM), NOT backed by the shared mmap, so the sidecars are the only road their content travels; QEMU's raw geometry must be synced (`-readconfig` on the driver path, `-global` in tests/e2e.sh -- HVM's property is `hvm_size_pow_2`, log2) because QEMU's compiled-in defaults (2 MB ILM at 0x0, 1-BYTE HVM) are wrong for every engine.

Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`, `HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT`, `HYBRID_FLAG_L2C`, `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (in the external vsim repo).

### V-State Transport

V data registers (v0..v31) move through a scratch region in the shared mmap.
L26: that region is the mmap's TOP page, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) =
ram_base + ram_size - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`, NOT a fixed address. The driver
maps one page more than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes`), so the
scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size`, just above the program's RAM, where no
program layout can collide with it (`cmd_run` also rejects an ELF whose static
image would reach into it). `ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain` take the GPA as a
required-when-V argument (the simulator passes `v_scratch_gpa()`); a V handoff
with it unset throws. vsim drives the transfer via the Debug Module **Program
Buffer** while the hart is halted, so benchmark binaries issue no transport code:
- `stage_v_to_scratch` copies `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` into the scratch region
  before resume; `ResumeDriver` then sweeps `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch into the
  regfile (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=true).
- At drain, `StateDrain` sweeps `vse8.v v0..v31` from the regfile back to scratch
  (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=false); `read_v_from_scratch` lifts the bytes into
  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` (the drained handoff file; there is no QEMU2 ship step).

Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m8 (vl=8*vlenb), which also forces vstart=0;
with LMUL=8 one `vle8.v`/`vse8.v` moves a group of 8 registers, so all 32 move in
4 grouped ops in a single Program-Buffer execution. The scratch is packed at the
RUNTIME vlenb stride (`stage_v_to_scratch` drops the wire-format
`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` padding so each 8-register group is contiguous).

V scalar CSR transport (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr):
- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS
- **Tier B** (Program Buffer): vtype + vl via `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` (direct CSR write to vtype sets vill; vl is read-only; only `vsetvl` restores both atomically)

Restore order in `ResumeDriver::resume()` when `HYBRID_FLAG_V` is set:
1. `mstatus.VS` (enables V in the hart)
2. V-data reload sweep: `vsetvl` e8/m8 then `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch in the
   Program Buffer. Runs BEFORE the architectural V-CSR restore (whose `vsetvl`
   overwrites the sweep's vtype/vl/vstart) and uses x5/x6/x7 as scratch.
3. `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in Program Buffer (stages `vl` in x5, `vtype` in x6 via abstract GPR writes first)
4. `vstart` (AFTER vsetvl: vsetvl resets vstart to 0)
5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)

`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` issues the matching `vse8.v` dump sweep
LAST, after every architectural read (GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret), so the
sweep's clobbers and any counter increments cannot corrupt the drained state.

### Test Fixtures

All fixtures run on the unified `tests/e2e.sh` harness, which
sets up an `/dev/shm`-backed shared mmap (128 MB) so memory survives
the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. Three fixture families:

| Family   | Examples                                                    | Notes |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
| asm      | `handoff_roundtrip`, `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_shared_mem` | no C runtime; don't strictly need shared mmap but use it anyway (~20 ms cost is negligible). |
| C-level  | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`   | hybrid round-trip tests, linked through the vplat runtime (below). Shared mmap is REQUIRED -- vsim resumes on QEMU1's memory, so the stack/heap and `main()`'s frame must survive the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. |
| vplat    | `vplat_hello`, `vplat_exit41`, `vplat_file`                 | smoke tests for the runtime's own features (exit code, file io). The runtime is engine-portable, shipped as `build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a` (sources in `runtime/`; build with `make -C runtime` or `scripts/build_all.sh runtime`): UART stdio + SimControl exit + HTIF file io, NO semihosting -- the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. Users link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. See docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 4; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`. |

The shared mmap is created with `mktemp -p /dev/shm` + `truncate`,
then QEMU is launched with `-object memory-backend-file`.

Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`; the shared runtime sources live at the repo root in `runtime/`. ALL C fixtures (rt_c_* and vplat_*) link through the shipped vplat runtime with the user command (`-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`); nothing in-tree links `-lgloss_vh` or uses semihosting syscalls anymore (asm fixtures still carry a semihosting exit fallback from `semihost_exit.inc`). V-using fixtures require `-march=rv64gcv`. Syscalls bottom out in MMIO devices both engines model (UART2 `0xf0300000`, SimControl/HTIF `0xe0080000` -- QEMU side is inline in `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c`), so a `printf` inside the ROI works on every engine (it just adds the real UART cycles to the figure); the old "Phase-2 no-syscall rule" survives only as a measurement-hygiene convention in cycle-measuring fixtures, and as a hard rule for user binaries that still link a semihosting libgloss. The ROI markers are HINT NOPs, so vplat binaries may carry them (`<andesim/ROI.h>`, installed to `build/runtime/include/`) and still run standalone on every engine; binaries you cannot edit delimit the ROI with PC symbols and `--trigger pc` instead.

## Key Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` | Wire-format struct (shared by all three components) |
| `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | TCG plugin: drain on trigger |
| `src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` (vsim repo) | Phase dispatcher |

| `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` (vsim repo) | CTest registration for the hybrid doctest unit tests |
| `scripts/run_e2e.sh` | Parallel e2e runner (FIFO job pool, per-test logs) |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runtime-lib F2 contract: `make -C runtime` produces a linkable library
# under build/runtime/ so users stop listing the 4 runtime sources:
#
#   build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a   (trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o)
#   build/runtime/crt0.o                   (startfile; OUTSIDE the archive)
#   build/runtime/andesim.ld             (linker script)
#
# Probe: link vplat_hello.c with the raw library line (no specs file yet)
# and run it on the cycle engine -- prints via UART, exits 0 via SimControl.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
NM="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" || fail "runtime lib build failed"

RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -f "$RT/libandesim_runtime.a" ] || fail "missing $RT/libandesim_runtime.a"
[ -f "$RT/crt0.o" ] || fail "missing $RT/crt0.o"
[ -f "$RT/andesim.ld" ] || fail "missing $RT/andesim.ld"

# crt0 must be a standalone startfile: the archive never gets _start pulled.
# (grep without -q: early-exit + pipefail turns a MATCH into SIGPIPE failure)
"$NM" "$RT/crt0.o" | grep ' T _start' >/dev/null \
  || fail "crt0.o does not define _start"
"$NM" "$RT/libandesim_runtime.a" | grep ' T _write' >/dev/null \
  || fail "archive does not define _write"
"$NM" "$RT/libandesim_runtime.a" | grep ' T m_trap_entry' >/dev/null \
  || fail "archive does not define m_trap_entry"

# Raw (non-specs) link: what a non-gcc-driver build system would write.
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs \
  -T "$RT/andesim.ld" "$RT/crt0.o" "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c" \
  -L "$RT" -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group \
  -o "$TMP/hello.elf" || fail "raw -landesim_runtime link failed"

OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from vplat' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F4 contract: HTIF file syscalls behave identically on both engines. The
# SAME vplat_file.elf creates/writes/reads/removes a host file (served by
# vsim's sim_control HTIF table and by QEMU's andes_sim_control mirror),
# prints "file io ok" and exits 0. Run in a scratch cwd; the tmp file must
# be gone afterwards (remove() worked host-side).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_file.elf"
SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
QEMU="${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"
[ -x "$QEMU" ] || fail "qemu not found (source ./setup.sh): $QEMU"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_file.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"

run_leg() {  # LABEL CMD...
  local label="$1"; shift
  local wd out rc
  wd=$(mktemp -d)
  out=$( cd "$wd" && timeout 120 "$@" </dev/null 2>&1 ); rc=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'file io ok' \
    || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: missing 'file io ok': $out"; }
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: exit code $rc != 0"; }
  [ ! -e "$wd/vplat_file_test.tmp" ] \
    || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: tmp file not removed"; }
  rm -rf "$wd"
  echo "[ok] $label: file io ok, clean exit, tmp removed"
}

run_leg cycle "$SIM" "$ELF"
run_leg fast "$QEMU" -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios "$ELF"

# rv32 leg (guarded): on rv32 the tohost command reaches the device as TWO
# 32-bit halves (0x10 low, 0x14 high) instead of one 64-bit store, so it
# exercises a distinct device path. Skips when the rv32 toolchain, runtime,
# or qemu-system-riscv32 is absent.
QEMU32="${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv32"
GCC32="$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc"
if [ -x "$QEMU32" ] && [ -x "$GCC32" ] && [ -d "$ROOT/build/runtime/rv32" ]; then
  ELF32=$(mktemp -t vplat_file32.XXXXXX.elf)
  "$GCC32" -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -B "$ROOT/build/runtime/rv32" \
    -specs=andesim.specs "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_file.c" -o "$ELF32" \
    || fail "rv32 fixture build failed"
  run_leg fast-rv32 "$QEMU32" -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-a45 \
    -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios "$ELF32"
  rm -f "$ELF32"
else
  echo "[skip] fast-rv32 leg: rv32 toolchain/runtime/qemu not available"
fi

ok "F4 vplat_file.elf HTIF file io parity (cycle + fast, incl. rv32 halves)"

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env ("" when neither is set).
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR
}

1	# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
2	#
3	# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
4	# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
5	# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
6	# to bypass the env var.
7	
8	TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
9	# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
10	# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
11	# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
12	rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
13	CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
14	LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
15	OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
16	
17	# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
18	# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
19	# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
20	RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
21	LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
22	# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
23	HELPERS_DIR := runtime
24	
25	CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
26	LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static
27	
28	# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
29	RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
30	               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
31	               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
32	               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
33	
34	# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
35	# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
36	# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
37	BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
38	                  break_verify_diverge
39	
40	# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
41	# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
42	# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
43	# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
44	# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
45	# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
46	# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
47	# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
48	# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
49	# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
50	RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
51	                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
52	RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
53	                    rt_c_hvm_data
54	RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file
55	
56	RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
57	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
58	# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
59	RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
60	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
61	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
62	VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
63	VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
64	                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
65	                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
66	VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
67	# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
68	# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
69	# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
70	VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
71	
72	# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
73	# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
74	# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
75	# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
76	# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
77	TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
78	CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
79	LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
80	CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
81	VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
82	VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
83	VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
84	                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
85	                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
86	
87	.PHONY: all clean dump rv32
88	
89	all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
90	     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
91	     hvm_readback.elf \
92	     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
93	     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
94	     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)
95	
96	# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
97	# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
98	# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.
99	
100	spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
101		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
102		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@
103	
104	handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
105		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
106		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@
107	
108	# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
109	# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
110	# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
111	# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
112	l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
113		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
114		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
115	lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
116	
117	# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
118	# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
119	# the exit code).
120	lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
121	                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
122		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
123	
124	# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
125	# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
126	hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
127		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
128	
129	$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
130		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
131		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
132	
133	# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
134	# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
135	$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
136		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
137		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
138	
139	# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
140	# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
141	$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
142		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
143		  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
144	
145	# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
146	# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
147	$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
148		$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
149		  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
150	rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
151	
152	# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
153	# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
154	$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
155		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
156	
157	# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
158	$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
159		$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)
160	
161	# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
162	# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
163	# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
164	# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
165	# same GEMM kernel.
166	rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
167		$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
168		  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@
169	
170	# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
171	rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf
172	
173	rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
174		$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
175		$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@
176	
177	rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
178		$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
179		  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@
180	
181	# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
182	$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
183		$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)
184	
185	dump: spin.elf
186		$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
187	
188	clean:
189		rm -f spin.o spin.elf \
190		      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
191		      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \
192		      lm_drain.o lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
                    rt_c_hvm_data
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
# the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \
	      lm_drain.o lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gettimeofday() must succeed on every vsim engine, not just the default.
# ax66_makatau's mmsc_cfg reports PL2C (L2 cache) support even though its
# build has zero L2 KB configured; vplat_syscalls.c's flush_dcache(), run
# before every HTIF syscall, must not treat that as "safe to touch the L2

# probe there fails before the ROI even starts.
set -uo pipefail

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_gettimeofday.elf >/dev/null \
  || fail "fixture build failed"

run_leg() {  # LABEL CMD...
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  out=$(timeout 120 "$@" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'gettimeofday ok' \
    || fail "$label: missing 'gettimeofday ok': $out"
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "$label: exit code $rc != 0 (output: $out)"
  echo "[ok] $label: gettimeofday ok, clean exit"
}

for eng in ax45mpv_premium ax46mpv_advanced ax66_makatau; do
  SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_$eng"
  [ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"
  run_leg "cycle:$eng" "$SIM" "$ELF"
done

  -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios "$ELF"

ok "gettimeofday.elf succeeds on every vsim engine + fast"

{
  __asm__ __volatile__("csrw mcctlcommand, %0" ::"rK"(6));
#if __riscv_xlen == 64

static void flush_dcache(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("csrw mcctlcommand, %0" ::"rK"(6));

  /* L2 writeback, gated to rv64 because it uses rv64-only ld/sd to reach the

   * (e.g. ax66_makatau) hardwire it to 1 even when built with zero L2 KB.

  __asm__ __volatile__(

static void flush_dcache(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("csrw mcctlcommand, %0" ::"rK"(6));
#if __riscv_xlen == 64
  /* DIAGNOSTIC: unconditionally skip the L2 flush to isolate whether this
   * block is the actual cause of the ax66_makatau gettimeofday failure.
   * NOT a real fix -- vplat_syscalls.c ROOT_CAUSE_DIAGNOSTIC in progress. */
  __asm__ __volatile__("j 3f\n");
  /* L2 writeback, gated to rv64 because it uses rv64-only ld/sd to reach the
   * 64-bit L2C MMIO registers (mmsc_cfg bit 46 is the L2-present flag) -- it
   * cannot COMPILE on rv32. Whether to flush is still decided at runtime by the
   * bit-46 check inside the asm. An rv32 core WITH an L2C would need a
   * 32-bit-halves access path here; today's rv32 target (d23) has no L2, so the
   * L1 writeback above suffices. */
  __asm__ __volatile__(
    "csrr    t0, mmsc_cfg\n"
    "li      t1, 1\n"
    "slli    t1, t1, 46\n"
    "and     t2, t0, t1\n"
    "beqz    t2, 1f\n"
    "li      t3, 0xe0500008\n"   /* L2C_REG_CTL: enabled? */
    "ld      t4, 0(t3)\n"
    "andi    t4, t4, 1\n"
    "beqz    t4, 1f\n"
    "li      t5, 0xe0500040\n"   /* L2C_REG_CCTL <- WBINVAL_ALL */
    "li      t6, 0x12\n"
    "sd      t6, 0(t5)\n"
    "2:\n"
    "li      t2, 0xe0500080\n"   /* poll L2C_REG_CCTL_M0_ST until idle */
    "ld      t3, 0(t2)\n"
    "andi    t3, t3, 0xF\n"
    "li      t5, 1\n"
    "beq     t3, t5, 2b\n"
    "1:\n" ::: "t0", "t1", "t2", "t3", "t4", "t5", "t6", "memory");
  __asm__ __volatile__("3:\n");
#endif
}

1	---
2	name: ax66-makatau-syscall-bug
3	description: vsim:ax66_makatau engine fails demo/syscall in --mode cycle due to a real bug in the andesim repo (not andesim-demo)
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 2f3f544d-3989-4811-a594-f467b83e9ab4
8	---
9	
10	`make check-all-engines` (in andesim-demo) sweeps all 3 vsim engines
11	(`ax45mpv_premium`, `ax46mpv_advanced`, `ax66_makatau`) and found
12	`vsim:ax66_makatau` fails `demo/syscall` in `--mode cycle`: the guest's
13	first-ever syscall, `gettimeofday()`, fails right after boot
14	(`SYSCALL_STAGE_BAD gettimeofday`, exit 2). The other two engines and
15	`--mode fast` pass fine.
16	
17	Root cause, verified by reading source directly (2026-07-13):
18	- `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c:72-103` (`flush_dcache()`, called by
19	  every `htif_syscall()`) checks CSR `mmsc_cfg` bit 46 ("L2 present").

---
name: ax66-makatau-syscall-bug
description: vsim:ax66_makatau engine fails demo/syscall in --mode cycle due to a real bug in the andesim repo (not andesim-demo)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 2f3f544d-3989-4811-a594-f467b83e9ab4
---

`make check-all-engines` (in andesim-demo) sweeps all 3 vsim engines
(`ax45mpv_premium`, `ax46mpv_advanced`, `ax66_makatau`) and found
`vsim:ax66_makatau` fails `demo/syscall` in `--mode cycle`: the guest's
first-ever syscall, `gettimeofday()`, fails right after boot
(`SYSCALL_STAGE_BAD gettimeofday`, exit 2). The other two engines and
`--mode fast` pass fine.

Root cause, verified by reading source directly (2026-07-13):
- `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c:72-103` (`flush_dcache()`, called by
  every `htif_syscall()`) checks CSR `mmsc_cfg` bit 46 ("L2 present").
  If set, it touches L2C control registers at `0xe0500008/40/80` with
  64-bit `ld`/`sd`.
- `ax66_makatau` is the only one of the 3 engines whose RTL decoder
  reports that bit as 1 (`tests/engines/ax66_makatau-5937b880/rtl_params.json`:
  `PL2C_SUPPORT: 1`; the other two engines have no such param at all).
- But `andesim/driver/memmap.hpp:22-24` and
  `andesim/docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md` problem M2 both say
  NO current engine actually has the L2C hardware built
  (`_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` everywhere, ax66_makatau included). So this
  engine's capability CSR says "L2 present" while the hardware disagrees.
- Guest trusts the CSR bit, touches a register that isn't really there
  -> breaks the HTIF syscall protocol on the very first syscall call.
- Second, independent bug in the same function: same doc's problem M5
  says L2C registers need <8-byte access (`sw`/`lwu`), but the code uses
  64-bit `ld`/`sd` regardless.

**CONFIRMED: not an RTL bug, it's a software bug (2026-07-13 follow-up).**
Checked `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/external/ax66/andes_ip/mk_core/ucore/csr/hdl/mk_csr.v`
directly. Line 433: `localparam PL2C_SUPPORT = 1; //*always support PL2C
for AX66 even if SIZE = 0KB` - this is an explicit, intentional vendor
design choice, not an oversight. Every other cache support flag in this
file IS size-gated (e.g. `ICACHE_SUPPORT = (ICACHE_SIZE_KB > 0) ? 1 :
0`); PL2C_SUPPORT is the one deliberate exception. The actually-correct,
size-aware CSR is `MPL2CM_CFG` (0xfdf): its `dsz`/`dway` fields are
properly gated on `PL2C_SIZE_KB == 0` (line 14818-14824, "no pl2
cache"). `PL2C_SIZE_KB` itself is a real configurable `parameter`
(line 280) currently 0 for this build - consistent with andesim's
`_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` claim.

So: `mmsc_cfg`'s coarse PL2C "support" bit is genuinely, deliberately 1
on ax66_makatau regardless of size; the RTL exposes the real answer
("is there actually a cache") through a different CSR
(`MPL2CM_CFG`/dsz-dway), which the andesim guest code never reads. The
bug is 100% in `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`'s `flush_dcache()`:
it must not treat the coarse support bit as "safe to touch L2C MMIO",
either checking `MPL2CM_CFG`'s size fields first, or another safe
gate.

(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`), a sibling repo to `andesim-demo` (this
project) - not something to fix inside andesim-demo. `andesim-demo`'s
own `check-all-engines` tooling (ROADMAP item 4, already DONE) is
working exactly as designed by catching this.

**How to apply:** if asked again to test/sweep engines, expect this
exact failure on `ax66_makatau` until `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`
is fixed to check `MPL2CM_CFG` size fields (not just `mmsc_cfg`'s PL2C
bit) before touching L2C MMIO, and/or fixes the `ld`/`sd` access width
to `sw`/`lwu` per spec. Root cause is now fully resolved/confirmed -
no need to re-investigate the RTL side again. User has not yet said
whether to apply the fix (cross-repo, in andesim) - ask before editing
that repo.

---
name: ax66-makatau-syscall-bug
description: vsim:ax66_makatau fails HTIF syscalls (gettimeofday, file io) in --mode cycle; root cause still NOT confirmed, first theory was empirically disproven
metadata:
  type: project
---

`make check-all-engines` (in andesim-demo) sweeps all 3 vsim engines
(`ax45mpv_premium`, `ax46mpv_advanced`, `ax66_makatau`) and found
`vsim:ax66_makatau` fails `demo/syscall` in `--mode cycle`: the guest's
first-ever syscall, `gettimeofday()`, fails right after boot
(`SYSCALL_STAGE_BAD gettimeofday` / `GETTIMEOFDAY: call failed`). The
other two engines and `--mode fast` pass fine.

**FIRST THEORY, DISPROVEN BY DIRECT TEST (2026-07-13).** Originally
suspected `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`'s `flush_dcache()`: it
checks `mmsc_cfg` bit 46 (PL2C_SUPPORT) and, if set, touches L2 cache
control MMIO at `0xe0500008/40/80`. Theory was that ax66_makatau's
build has this capability bit set but no real L2 cache, so the MMIO
touch breaks things. **This is WRONG and was proven wrong empirically:**
- Checked the ACTUAL BUILT RTL config (not just the generic vendor
  template): `vsim_andesim/build/Vax66_makatau/obj_sc/config.inc:156`
  sets `NDS_PL2C_SIZE_KB=256` - ax66_makatau genuinely HAS a real
  256KB L2 cache. The `andesim` repo's own docs
  (`driver/memmap.hpp`, `docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md` M2,
  saying "every engine built with L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0") are STALE for
  this engine - written before ax66_makatau was added and never
  updated. Don't trust those two doc locations for this engine.
- Wrote a real RED/GREEN test (`tests/fixtures/vplat_gettimeofday.c` +
  `tests/vplat/test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh`, committed to neither repo
  yet, still on disk in `andesim`). Bisected by (a) adding an
  `MPL2CM_CFG`-based gate mirroring the (wrong) theory - no change; (b)
  unconditionally skipping the ENTIRE L2 flush block - ax66_makatau
  STILL fails identically; (c) neutering `flush_dcache()` completely
  including the L1 `mcctlcommand` write - this broke `ax45mpv_premium`
  too (`invalid syscall number 0`, confirming the L1 flush is genuinely
  load-bearing/necessary), while ax66_makatau's failure mode stayed
  distinct. Conclusion: `flush_dcache()`/L2 is NOT the cause. All
  edits were reverted; `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c` is back to its
  original committed state (verified via `git diff`, clean).

**New evidence (broader than gettimeofday alone).** Ran existing
fixtures directly against `sim_ax66_makatau`:
- `vplat_hello.elf` (UART printf only, no HTIF magicmem) - PASSES.
- `vplat_exit41.elf` (SimControl exit only, no HTIF magicmem) - PASSES.
- `vplat_file.elf` (fopen/fwrite/fread/fclose/remove - ALL route
  through `htif_syscall()`/`magicmem[]`) - HARD CRASH, not a clean
  failure: `[critical] target socket not found for address
  0x6300050980` (a SystemC/TLM bus error - that address is nonsense,
  ~426GB, nothing like a real DRAM address) followed by an actual CPU
  trap (`mcause: 0x2`, `mepc: 0x10` - also a nonsense PC). This is a
  more SEVERE failure than gettimeofday's clean `return 1`.
- Working theory (UNCONFIRMED): the bug is in `htif_syscall()`'s
  `magicmem[]`/HTIF MMIO trigger mechanism itself on this engine - not
  in `flush_dcache()` specifically - and may be a vsim-side platform/
  SoC-integration gap for this new engine (a third repo,
  `vsim_andesim`, not `andesim`), not fixable by guest-side runtime
  code alone. NOT YET VERIFIED. Do not assume this is right either -
  it is the next lead, not a conclusion.

**Why this matters:** two wrong turns already burned real effort in
one session. The lesson: for this specific bug, static RTL/doc reading
was NOT sufficient and actively misleading (the "every engine has 0KB
L2" doc claim was stale) - empirical bisection (running real ELFs
against the real engine binary) is what actually falsified the theory.
Any future work on this MUST re-verify against a running engine before
trusting doc comments in either repo.

**How to apply:** if asked to test/fix this again, do NOT restate the
old "PL2C_SUPPORT/L2 cache" theory as fact - it's disproven. Start from
the `vplat_file.elf` crash evidence above. Test fixtures
(`vplat_gettimeofday.c`/`test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh`) already exist on
disk in `andesim` (uncommitted) and reproduce the gettimeofday-specific
failure cleanly - reuse them rather than rewriting. User has not yet
been told this investigation is now open-ended/harder than originally
scoped - say so before continuing further, and ask whether to keep
digging (likely needs vsim_andesim platform/testbench source) or stop.

name: ax66-makatau-syscall-bug
description: vsim:ax66_makatau engine fails demo/syscall in --mode cycle due to a real bug in the andesim repo (not andesim-demo)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 2f3f544d-3989-4811-a594-f467b83e9ab4

`make check-all-engines` (in andesim-demo) sweeps all 3 vsim engines
(`ax45mpv_premium`, `ax46mpv_advanced`, `ax66_makatau`) and found
`vsim:ax66_makatau` fails `demo/syscall` in `--mode cycle`: the guest's
first-ever syscall, `gettimeofday()`, fails right after boot
(`SYSCALL_STAGE_BAD gettimeofday`, exit 2). The other two engines and
`--mode fast` pass fine.

Root cause, verified by reading source directly (2026-07-13):
- `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c:72-103` (`flush_dcache()`, called by
  every `htif_syscall()`) checks CSR `mmsc_cfg` bit 46 ("L2 present").
  If set, it touches L2C control registers at `0xe0500008/40/80` with
  64-bit `ld`/`sd`.
- `ax66_makatau` is the only one of the 3 engines whose RTL decoder
  reports that bit as 1 (`tests/engines/ax66_makatau-5937b880/rtl_params.json`:
  `PL2C_SUPPORT: 1`; the other two engines have no such param at all).
- But `andesim/driver/memmap.hpp:22-24` and
  `andesim/docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md` problem M2 both say
  NO current engine actually has the L2C hardware built
  (`_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` everywhere, ax66_makatau included). So this
  engine's capability CSR says "L2 present" while the hardware disagrees.
- Guest trusts the CSR bit, touches a register that isn't really there
  -> breaks the HTIF syscall protocol on the very first syscall call.
- Second, independent bug in the same function: same doc's problem M5
  says L2C registers need <8-byte access (`sw`/`lwu`), but the code uses
  64-bit `ld`/`sd` regardless.

**CONFIRMED: not an RTL bug, it's a software bug (2026-07-13 follow-up).**
Checked `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/external/ax66/andes_ip/mk_core/ucore/csr/hdl/mk_csr.v`
directly. Line 433: `localparam PL2C_SUPPORT = 1; //*always support PL2C
for AX66 even if SIZE = 0KB` - this is an explicit, intentional vendor
design choice, not an oversight. Every other cache support flag in this
file IS size-gated (e.g. `ICACHE_SUPPORT = (ICACHE_SIZE_KB > 0) ? 1 :
0`); PL2C_SUPPORT is the one deliberate exception. The actually-correct,
size-aware CSR is `MPL2CM_CFG` (0xfdf): its `dsz`/`dway` fields are
properly gated on `PL2C_SIZE_KB == 0` (line 14818-14824, "no pl2
cache"). `PL2C_SIZE_KB` itself is a real configurable `parameter`
(line 280) currently 0 for this build - consistent with andesim's
`_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` claim.

So: `mmsc_cfg`'s coarse PL2C "support" bit is genuinely, deliberately 1
on ax66_makatau regardless of size; the RTL exposes the real answer
("is there actually a cache") through a different CSR
(`MPL2CM_CFG`/dsz-dway), which the andesim guest code never reads. The
bug is 100% in `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`'s `flush_dcache()`:
it must not treat the coarse support bit as "safe to touch L2C MMIO",
either checking `MPL2CM_CFG`'s size fields first, or another safe
gate.

**Why this matters:** the bug lives in `/home/nick/work/andesim`
(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`), a sibling repo to `andesim-demo` (this
project) - not something to fix inside andesim-demo. `andesim-demo`'s
own `check-all-engines` tooling (ROADMAP item 4, already DONE) is
working exactly as designed by catching this.

**How to apply:** if asked again to test/sweep engines, expect this
exact failure on `ax66_makatau` until `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`
is fixed to check `MPL2CM_CFG` size fields (not just `mmsc_cfg`'s PL2C
bit) before touching L2C MMIO, and/or fixes the `ld`/`sd` access width
to `sw`/`lwu` per spec. Root cause is now fully resolved/confirmed -
no need to re-investigate the RTL side again. User has not yet said
whether to apply the fix (cross-repo, in andesim) - ask before editing
that repo.

content.text:
My first fix was wrong. I tested it, and the bug is still there — and it's bigger than I thought.

**What I did:**
1. Made a real test (following proper test-first practice): a small program that just calls `gettimeofday()`, run on all 3 chips. It failed only on `ax66_makatau`, exactly as expected.
2. Applied my fix (the "read Sign B" idea from before). Rebuilt. Ran the test again.
3. **It still failed. Same error, almost same speed.** My fix did nothing.

**So I checked deeper, and found my last explanation was wrong:**

I checked the REAL chip build files (not just the generic template I read before). Turns out `ax66_makatau` really DOES have a real 256KB cache built in. It's not "pretending to have a cache" like I said last time — it genuinely has one. So "Sign A says yes, Sign B says no" was not actually true. I was wrong.

**Then I tested something bigger, and found the problem is not just about `gettimeofday`:**

I ran other, already-working test programs directly against this same chip:
- A program that only prints text → works fine.
- A program that only exits with a number → works fine.
- A program that reads/writes a FILE (open, write, read, close) → **crashes hard.** Not a clean "failed", a real crash: the chip simulator says "target socket not found for address 0x6300050980" (a nonsense address, way too big to be real) and the processor itself traps.

So the real pattern is: **anything that talks to the host computer through this one specific channel (called HTIF) breaks on this chip** — `gettimeofday` is just the FIRST thing in line that uses that channel, so it's the first thing to break. It's not a small, one-function bug anymore.

**I undid all my code changes.** The file is back to exactly how it was before (I checked with `git diff` — no changes left).

This looks like it may be a problem in the CHIP SIMULATOR itself (a third project folder, `vsim_andesim` — the actual hardware simulation, not the `andesim` driver code), not something I can fix by editing `vplat_syscalls.c` alone. That's a bigger, harder investigation than I first thought.

Do you want me to keep digging (this means reading chip-simulator code, which is a different kind of investigation), or stop here for now?

---
name: ax66-makatau-syscall-bug
description: "vsim:ax66_makatau fails HTIF syscalls (gettimeofday, file io) in --mode cycle; root cause still NOT confirmed, first theory was empirically disproven"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 2f3f544d-3989-4811-a594-f467b83e9ab4
---

`make check-all-engines` (in andesim-demo) sweeps all 3 vsim engines
(`ax45mpv_premium`, `ax46mpv_advanced`, `ax66_makatau`) and found
`vsim:ax66_makatau` fails `demo/syscall` in `--mode cycle`: the guest's
first-ever syscall, `gettimeofday()`, fails right after boot
(`SYSCALL_STAGE_BAD gettimeofday` / `GETTIMEOFDAY: call failed`). The
other two engines and `--mode fast` pass fine.

**FIRST THEORY, DISPROVEN BY DIRECT TEST (2026-07-13).** Originally
suspected `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`'s `flush_dcache()`: it
checks `mmsc_cfg` bit 46 (PL2C_SUPPORT) and, if set, touches L2 cache
control MMIO at `0xe0500008/40/80`. Theory was that ax66_makatau's
build has this capability bit set but no real L2 cache, so the MMIO
touch breaks things. **This is WRONG and was proven wrong empirically:**
- Checked the ACTUAL BUILT RTL config (not just the generic vendor
  template): `vsim_andesim/build/Vax66_makatau/obj_sc/config.inc:156`
  sets `NDS_PL2C_SIZE_KB=256` - ax66_makatau genuinely HAS a real
  256KB L2 cache. The `andesim` repo's own docs
  (`driver/memmap.hpp`, `docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md` M2,
  saying "every engine built with L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0") are STALE for
  this engine - written before ax66_makatau was added and never
  updated. Don't trust those two doc locations for this engine.
- Wrote a real RED/GREEN test (`tests/fixtures/vplat_gettimeofday.c` +
  `tests/vplat/test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh`, committed to neither repo
  yet, still on disk in `andesim`). Bisected by (a) adding an
  `MPL2CM_CFG`-based gate mirroring the (wrong) theory - no change; (b)
  unconditionally skipping the ENTIRE L2 flush block - ax66_makatau
  STILL fails identically; (c) neutering `flush_dcache()` completely
  including the L1 `mcctlcommand` write - this broke `ax45mpv_premium`
  too (`invalid syscall number 0`, confirming the L1 flush is genuinely
  load-bearing/necessary), while ax66_makatau's failure mode stayed
  distinct. Conclusion: `flush_dcache()`/L2 is NOT the cause. All
  edits were reverted; `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c` is back to its
  original committed state (verified via `git diff`, clean).

**New evidence (broader than gettimeofday alone).** Ran existing
fixtures directly against `sim_ax66_makatau`:
- `vplat_hello.elf` (UART printf only, no HTIF magicmem) - PASSES.
- `vplat_exit41.elf` (SimControl exit only, no HTIF magicmem) - PASSES.
- `vplat_file.elf` (fopen/fwrite/fread/fclose/remove - ALL route
  through `htif_syscall()`/`magicmem[]`) - HARD CRASH, not a clean
  failure: `[critical] target socket not found for address
  0x6300050980` (a SystemC/TLM bus error - that address is nonsense,
  ~426GB, nothing like a real DRAM address) followed by an actual CPU
  trap (`mcause: 0x2`, `mepc: 0x10` - also a nonsense PC). This is a
  more SEVERE failure than gettimeofday's clean `return 1`.
- Working theory (UNCONFIRMED): the bug is in `htif_syscall()`'s
  `magicmem[]`/HTIF MMIO trigger mechanism itself on this engine - not
  in `flush_dcache()` specifically - and may be a vsim-side platform/
  SoC-integration gap for this new engine (a third repo,
  `vsim_andesim`, not `andesim`), not fixable by guest-side runtime
  code alone. NOT YET VERIFIED. Do not assume this is right either -
  it is the next lead, not a conclusion.

**Why this matters:** two wrong turns already burned real effort in
one session. The lesson: for this specific bug, static RTL/doc reading
was NOT sufficient and actively misleading (the "every engine has 0KB
L2" doc claim was stale) - empirical bisection (running real ELFs
against the real engine binary) is what actually falsified the theory.
Any future work on this MUST re-verify against a running engine before
trusting doc comments in either repo.

**How to apply:** if asked to test/fix this again, do NOT restate the
old "PL2C_SUPPORT/L2 cache" theory as fact - it's disproven. Start from
the `vplat_file.elf` crash evidence above. Test fixtures
(`vplat_gettimeofday.c`/`test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh`) already exist on
disk in `andesim` (uncommitted) and reproduce the gettimeofday-specific
failure cleanly - reuse them rather than rewriting. User has not yet
been told this investigation is now open-ended/harder than originally
scoped - say so before continuing further, and ask whether to keep
digging (likely needs vsim_andesim platform/testbench source) or stop.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gettimeofday() must succeed on every vsim engine, not just the default.
# ax66_makatau's mmsc_cfg reports PL2C (L2 cache) support even though its
# build has zero L2 KB configured; vplat_syscalls.c's flush_dcache(), run
# before every HTIF syscall, must not treat that as "safe to touch the L2
# MMIO window" -- gettimeofday is the runtime's first syscall, so a bad
# probe there fails before the ROI even starts.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_gettimeofday.elf"
QEMU="${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64"
[ -x "$QEMU" ] || fail "qemu not found (source ./setup.sh): $QEMU"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_gettimeofday.elf >/dev/null \
  || fail "fixture build failed"

run_leg() {  # LABEL CMD...
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  out=$(timeout 120 "$@" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'gettimeofday ok' \
    || fail "$label: missing 'gettimeofday ok': $out"
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "$label: exit code $rc != 0 (output: $out)"
  echo "[ok] $label: gettimeofday ok, clean exit"
}

for eng in ax45mpv_premium ax46mpv_advanced ax66_makatau; do
  SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_$eng"
  [ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"
  run_leg "cycle:$eng" "$SIM" "$ELF"
done

run_leg fast "$QEMU" -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios "$ELF"

ok "gettimeofday.elf succeeds on every vsim engine + fast"

                    27.3.9            Simulation Control
                    Thesepatternsruninaself-checkmanner. Ifanunexpectederrorisdetected,theprogramwillwritea
                    speciﬁc value to ahb_sim_control to terminate the simulation early. If the test completes successfully,
                    the program writes another speciﬁc value to ahb_sim_control to gracefully terminate the simulation.
                    Onthehardware side, ahb_sim_control achieves this by snooping AHB trafﬁcs on the internal subor-
                    dinate (subordinate 0) of the AHB Decoder. This internal subordinate is allocated a 1 MiB space (see
                    Table 124) but uses less than two hundred bytes. By default, the BASE parameter of ahb_sim_control
                    is set to 0x80000, meaning it only checks offset addresses beyond 512 KiB in this 1 MiB space. This
                    guarantees the existence of ahb_sim_control will not interfere the normal operation of this internal
                    subordinate.
                    If the base memory address of this 1 MiB space is changed, the monitored space of ahb_sim_control
                    will also be changed, since the snooping relies directly on the internal signals after address decoding
                    inside the AHB Decoder. This 1 MiB space must reside in the device region, ensuring the memory
                    space of ahb_sim_control is also within the device region.
                    When ahb_sim_control detects an AHB write transaction to the BASE offset with certain recognized
                    values of write data, it prints related pass/fail information and calls Verilog system task $finish to

                    27.3.9            Simulation Control
                    Thesepatternsruninaself-checkmanner. Ifanunexpectederrorisdetected,theprogramwillwritea
                    speciﬁc value to ahb_sim_control to terminate the simulation early. If the test completes successfully,
                    the program writes another speciﬁc value to ahb_sim_control to gracefully terminate the simulation.
                    Onthehardware side, ahb_sim_control achieves this by snooping AHB trafﬁcs on the internal subor-
                    dinate (subordinate 0) of the AHB Decoder. This internal subordinate is allocated a 1 MiB space (see
                    Table 124) but uses less than two hundred bytes. By default, the BASE parameter of ahb_sim_control
                    is set to 0x80000, meaning it only checks offset addresses beyond 512 KiB in this 1 MiB space. This
                    guarantees the existence of ahb_sim_control will not interfere the normal operation of this internal
                    subordinate.
                    If the base memory address of this 1 MiB space is changed, the monitored space of ahb_sim_control
                    will also be changed, since the snooping relies directly on the internal signals after address decoding
                    inside the AHB Decoder. This 1 MiB space must reside in the device region, ensuring the memory
                    space of ahb_sim_control is also within the device region.
                    When ahb_sim_control detects an AHB write transaction to the BASE offset with certain recognized
                    values of write data, it prints related pass/fail information and calls Verilog system task $finish to
                    terminate the simulation. Details of ahb_sim_control are listed in Table 187.

---
name: ax66-makatau-syscall-bug
description: "vsim:ax66_makatau fails HTIF syscalls (gettimeofday, file io) in --mode cycle; spec confirms the syscall bridge is a non-vendor extension, root cause narrowed to vsim_andesim platform wiring"
metadata:
  type: project
---

`make check-all-engines` (in andesim-demo) sweeps all 3 vsim engines
(`ax45mpv_premium`, `ax46mpv_advanced`, `ax66_makatau`) and found
`vsim:ax66_makatau` fails `demo/syscall` in `--mode cycle`: the guest's
first-ever syscall, `gettimeofday()`, fails right after boot. The other
two engines and `--mode fast` pass fine.

**FIRST THEORY, DISPROVEN BY DIRECT TEST.** Suspected `flush_dcache()`'s
L2 MMIO writeback code (mmsc_cfg bit 46 gate) in
`andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`. Wrong - see bisection below. Do not
restate this as fact.

**Bisection evidence (empirical, from running real ELFs on
sim_ax66_makatau):**
- `vplat_hello.elf` (UART printf only) - PASSES.
- `vplat_exit41.elf` (SimControl exit only) - PASSES.
- `vplat_gettimeofday.c` (new fixture, uses HTIF magicmem) - FAILS.
- `vplat_file.elf` (fopen/fwrite/fread, uses HTIF magicmem) - HARD
  CRASH: SystemC/TLM "target socket not found for address
  0x6300050980" (nonsense ~426GB address) + CPU trap (mcause 0x2).
- Skipping flush_dcache()'s entire L2/L3 MMIO block: ax66_makatau
  STILL fails gettimeofday identically -> that block is NOT the cause.
- Neutering flush_dcache() completely (incl. the L1 `mcctlcommand`
  write): broke `ax45mpv_premium` too (proves L1 flush is genuinely
  load-bearing, unrelated to this bug).
- All diagnostic edits reverted; `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c` is back to
  its original committed state (verified clean via `git diff`).

**Two confirmed findings from reading the actual AX66 vendor datasheet**
(`andesim-demo/AndesCore_AX66_DS295_V0.4_interim.pdf`, converted to text
with `gs -sDEVICE=txtwrite` since no pdftotext/pdfgrep/PyMuPDF was
installed):

1. **Cosmetic bug, confirmed NOT the root cause.** `flush_dcache()`'s
   comment calls `mmsc_cfg` bit 46 the "L2-present flag"
   (`PL2C_SUPPORT`). The datasheet (Ch 19.5.3, register `mmsc_cfg`
   @0xfc2) names bit 46 `CCACHE` = "Indicates whether the cluster
   cache is present" - a SHARED/L3 cache flag, not the private-L2
   flag. The real private-L2 flag is a different CSR entirely:
   `mmsc_cfg3.PL2C` (bit 5 of CSR 0xfc4), gating `mpl2cm_cfg` (CSR
   0xfdf). The MMIO block the code actually touches at 0xE0500000
   (CCTL Command/Access-Line/Status Register 0, per Table 33 Ch 11.7)
   IS genuinely AX66's L3/"cluster cache" register block, and opcode
   `0x12` written there IS genuinely `L3_WBINVAL_ALL` (Table @
   Section 11.7.11/3206) - so the code's runtime gate and MMIO usage
   are functionally correct for this engine, just mis-commented
   ("L2" should say "cluster cache/L3"). Likely bit 46 meant
   `PL2C_SUPPORT` on the older kv_core family (ax45/ax46) and got
   reassigned to `CCACHE` in the new mk_core family (ax66) at the same
   bit position - a cross-generation CSR meaning collision. Confirmed
   via bisection this is NOT the crash cause (removing the whole block
   doesn't fix gettimeofday).

2. **The real lead.** The datasheet's OWN simulation-control chapter
   (Ch 27.3.9, Table 187 "Simulation Control Registers") documents
   `ahb_sim_control` as supporting exactly THREE write-only magic
   values at the AHB Decoder's BASE offset: finish (0x01234568), abort
   (0x01234569), skip (0x01234571). That's it - a bare pass/fail
   signal. Full-text search of the entire ~500-page datasheet for
   "HTIF", "magicmem", "TOHOST", "syscall" returns ZERO hits. **The
   richer file-io/gettimeofday syscall bridge
   (`HTIF_TOHOST_CMD`@0xe0080010 + `magicmem[8]` struct + syscall
   number table) that `vplat_syscalls.c` depends on is NOT part of
   AX66's vendor-documented IP at all.** It must be a custom
   Andes-simulation-team extension living in the `vsim_andesim` repo's
   own testbench/platform source (e.g. `sim_control.hpp`, named in
   `vplat_syscalls.c`'s own comments), layered on top of the vendor's
   bare-bones `ahb_sim_control`. This lines up exactly with the
   bisection split above: everything that passes (`vplat_hello`,
   `vplat_exit41`) uses only vendor-documented mechanisms (UART,
   ahb_sim_control exit); everything that fails
   (`vplat_gettimeofday`/`vplat_file`) uses the custom magicmem
   extension. Strong evidence the bug is in how `vsim_andesim`'s
   custom syscall-bridge code is wired onto the AX66 core/bus
   specifically (most likely a bus/socket-binding gap for this newest
   engine), not fixable in guest-side `vplat_syscalls.c`.

**Why this matters:** two wrong turns (this one plus the earlier L2
theory) already burned real effort. The lesson: for this bug, neither
guest-side code reading nor generic vendor-template reading was
enough - only (a) running real ELFs against the real engine binary and
(b) reading the ACTUAL vendor datasheet's own documented scope
actually narrowed this down. Trust neither doc comments nor vendor
templates without cross-checking against the real build/spec.

**How to apply:** if asked to continue, the next concrete step is
reading `vsim_andesim`'s own testbench/platform source for how the
custom HTIF/magicmem syscall bridge (likely `sim_control.hpp` or
equivalent) is bound onto the bus for `ax66_makatau` specifically,
compared to how it's bound for `ax45mpv_premium`/`ax46mpv_advanced`
(which work). That is a different repo and a different kind of
investigation (SystemC/TLM platform wiring) than anything done so far.
Test fixtures already exist on disk in `andesim` (uncommitted):
`tests/fixtures/vplat_gettimeofday.c` + `tests/vplat/test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh`
- reuse them. User has been told the investigation is open-ended;
last checkpoint was asking whether to keep digging into vsim_andesim
platform source or stop.

content.text:
I found something useful in the spec. Two things:

**1. A real but small mistake in the code's comment (not the crash cause).**

The code checks bit 46 of a chip register (`mmsc_cfg`) and calls it "L2 cache present." The spec says bit 46 is actually named `CCACHE` = "shared cache present" (a different cache, called L3). So the comment used the wrong name. But the actual memory addresses and commands the code sends ARE correct for this shared cache. This is just a wrong label, not a bug. And we already proved (last session) that removing this whole block doesn't fix the crash - so this isn't what's breaking things.

**2. The real clue.**

I read the official AX66 spec's own section about its "simulation control" feature (how a test program tells the simulator "I'm done, pass/fail"). The spec says this feature ONLY supports 3 simple signals: finish, abort, skip. Nothing else.

I searched the ENTIRE 500-page spec for words like "HTIF", "magicmem" (the mechanism our code uses for file reading/writing and getting the time) - **zero matches.**

This means: the file-read/write/time mechanism our code depends on is **not something the chip vendor built**. It must be something Andes' own simulator team added on top, in a different folder (`vsim_andesim`), separate from the official chip design.

This actually matches our test results perfectly:
- Programs using ONLY vendor features (print text, exit) → **work fine**
- Programs using the extra file/time mechanism → **crash**

So the bug is very likely in how that extra mechanism was connected to this specific new chip (`ax66_makatau`) inside `vsim_andesim` - probably a wiring mistake, not something we can fix in `vplat_syscalls.c`.

Want me to continue and look inside `vsim_andesim` for this wiring? That's a new folder and a different kind of code (simulator wiring, not chip design or our runtime code).

content.text:
One chip out of three (`ax66_makatau`) crashes on file read/write and "get current time." The other two chips are fine.

**The symptom:**
1. A test program starts, and the very first thing it does is ask for the current time (`gettimeofday`).
2. On `ax66_makatau`, this fails right away.
3. A harder test (reading/writing a file) doesn't just fail - it crashes the whole simulator. The error says it tried to reach a memory address that doesn't exist.
4. Simpler programs (just print text, or just exit) work fine on this same chip.

**So the pattern is:** "get time" and "file I/O" break. "Print text" and "exit" don't.

**What we know so far:** "get time" and "file I/O" both use one special mechanism. I checked the official chip spec (the PDF) and that mechanism is **not in the official chip design at all** - it must be something Andes' simulator team bolted on separately for each chip. "Print text" and "exit" use different, official mechanisms - and those work.

**What we don't know yet:** the exact reason that bolted-on mechanism is broken for this one chip. My best guess (not proven) is a wiring mistake made when this mechanism was connected to this specific new chip.

message.content: 不太懂 system call HTIF 不是由host 完成的? 跟RTL core 有什麼關係?

content.text:
You're right - the host does the actual work (reading the file, getting the time). But the request has to travel THROUGH the simulated chip's hardware first, to reach the host. That travel path is the part that can be broken.

**Analogy: a mailbox in the wall.**

- The guest program (running inside the simulated chip) is a person in a room.
- The host is a helper standing outside.
- To ask for help, the person puts a note in a mailbox built into the wall, then presses a doorbell next to it.
- The helper hears the doorbell, opens the mailbox, reads the note, does the task, and writes the answer back.

The mailbox and doorbell are physically part of the wall - built by the chip's hardware design (RTL / the simulator model). Each of the 3 chips has a DIFFERENT wall (different hardware design). The helper (host code) is the SAME for all 3.

If one wall's mailbox is wired wrong - the doorbell doesn't ring, or the mailbox is empty/broken when the helper checks - the note never arrives correctly. The helper is not broken. The wall is.

**Mapped to our real bug:**
- "Note in mailbox" = writing the request into memory (`magicmem`)
- "Doorbell" = writing to a special address (`HTIF_TOHOST_CMD`) that tells the host "go check now"
- "Helper reads the note" = host reads that memory directly, done by `vsim_andesim`'s simulator code
- Both steps depend on the chip's simulated wiring actually connecting memory + that special address to the host correctly

The vendor spec proved: the "doorbell" mechanism itself (mailbox + note format) isn't part of the official chip design - Andes' own simulator team built it separately for each chip. So it's very possible that for this one new chip (`ax66_makatau`), that wiring was built wrong or incomplete - which fits everything we've seen: simple things (print text, exit - different, official signals) work; anything using the mailbox (get time, file I/O) breaks.
