Repo to investigate: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim (a SystemC + Verilator RTL simulator for RISC-V chips, called "vsim"). This is READ-ONLY investigation - do not edit any files.

## Background

A separate repo (`andesim`, not this one) has guest-side runtime code at `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c` that implements a custom syscall bridge for programs running inside the simulator:
- The guest writes a request (syscall number + args) into a normal DRAM array called `magicmem[8]` (8 x uint64_t, 64-byte aligned).
- The guest then does a flush (writes back its D-cache so the write is visible outside the CPU), then writes the POINTER to `magicmem` into a fixed MMIO address `0xe0080010` (called `HTIF_TOHOST_CMD` in the guest code).
- The host/simulator side is supposed to notice this write, then read the `magicmem` struct directly from guest DRAM (bypassing the CPU's caches), service the request (gettimeofday, file open/read/write/close/stat/etc - see the syscall number table in vplat_syscalls.c for the full list: VH_SYS_GETTIMEOFDAY=5, VH_SYS_OPEN=6, VH_SYS_WRITE=7, VH_SYS_GETCWD=8, VH_SYS_LSEEK=9, VH_SYS_READ=10, VH_SYS_FLEN=11, VH_SYS_CLOSE=12, VH_SYS_ACCESS=13, VH_SYS_FACCESSAT=14, VH_SYS_FSTAT=15, VH_SYS_FSTATAT=16, VH_SYS_LINK=17, VH_SYS_LSTAT=18, VH_SYS_STAT=19, VH_SYS_OPENAT=20, VH_SYS_RENAME=21, VH_SYS_UNLINK=22), and write a result back into the struct.
- The guest code's own comments say this is implemented in a file called `sim_control.hpp` on the vsim (this repo's) side, and mirrored separately in QEMU (a different, unrelated repo/binary - ignore QEMU, focus only on vsim_andesim).

There's also a SEPARATE, simpler, vendor-documented mechanism (NOT the bug's focus, just for contrast): a "SimControl"/`ahb_sim_control` module at MMIO address `0xe0080000` that only accepts 3 write-only magic values (finish/abort/skip) to end a simulation. That one is known-good and works everywhere - not what you're investigating.

## Confirmed facts (from prior testing in this session, already verified empirically - trust these, don't re-derive them)

- This repo builds 3 separate RISC-V engines, each with its own build output directory under `build/`: `Vax45mpv_premium`, `Vax46mpv_advanced`, `Vax66_makatau` (exact directory names may vary slightly - verify).
- `ax66_makatau` is the NEWEST engine, first registration of a new core family internally called "mk_core" (the other two are an older "kv_core" family).
- On `ax45mpv_premium` and `ax46mpv_advanced`, the magicmem/HTIF syscall bridge works correctly (a test program calling gettimeofday() and doing file I/O succeeds).
- On `ax66_makatau` specifically, the SAME guest code fails: `gettimeofday()` fails cleanly (returns an error code, no crash), and file I/O (fopen/fwrite/fread/fclose) causes a HARD CRASH: a SystemC/TLM error message "target socket not found for address 0x6300050980" (note: that's a nonsensical address, ~426GB, nothing like a valid guest DRAM address) followed by a CPU trap (mcause 0x2, mepc 0x10 - also nonsensical, suggesting the CPU itself faulted).
- Things that do NOT use the magicmem/HTIF bridge (UART console printf, and the simple SimControl exit-only signal at 0xe0080000) work FINE on ax66_makatau. Only the magicmem/HTIF bridge is broken on this one engine.

  ```cpp
  auto addr_offset = cmd.payload() - data_region.region.base_address;   // line 221
  auto src = data_region.data.begin() + addr_offset;                   // line 222
  ```

```cpp
this->interconnect.bind_target(this->main_memory.socket, this->main_memory.region);
```

  ```cpp
  if (region.contains_access(addr, len)) offset = addr - this->region.base_address;
  ```

```cpp
const auto target = this->find_fw_if_from_address(addr);
if (!target) {
  spdlog::critical("target socket not found for address {:#x}, ...", addr, ...);
  trans.set_response_status(tlm::TLM_ADDRESS_ERROR_RESPONSE);
  ...
}
```
`find_fw_if_from_address` (lines 51-59) linearly scans every registered `(MemoryRegion, target)` pair and returns `nullptr` if none contains `addr`. This is a genuine TLM/AXI bus-level address-decode miss on an actual initiator-issued transaction - it fires only when the CPU (or a bridge acting for it) puts a real bus request on an address that no `bind_target`/`bind_target_no_check` call ever registered. It is architecturally distinct from `dispatch()`'s/`guest_va_to_host()`'s backdoor pointer math, which never creates a TLM transaction at all - the backdoor bug and this error are two different mechanisms that could plausibly interact (see caveat below), not the same code path.

### (d) Conclusion

**Concrete gap found, with direct evidence, not speculation**: `SimControl::dispatch()` (`src/platform/sim_control.hpp:218-225`) and `guest_va_to_host()` (`src/htif/sys_call.hpp:30-35`) translate a guest DRAM pointer into a host pointer using only `data_region.region.base_address`, and never consult `data_region.alias_region`, even though `SimpleMemory::handle_trans` (the code path used for ordinary bus reads/writes) and the interconnect both fully support and require alias-region awareness for ax66. ax66's own vendor sample `platform.h` sets `DDR3_MEM_BASE = 0x800000000` (vs `0x0` for ax45mpv_premium/ax46mpv_advanced), so ax66 guest pointers - including, presumably, the `magicmem` array's own address and any syscall buffer/string pointers - land in the alias window that the HTIF backdoor ignores. Git history shows the alias region was added in commit `17b42047` explicitly "useful for ax66" while deliberately not touching the HTIF files, and a later dedicated "HTIF VA fix" commit (`9f6fd84`) still only handled the unrelated Tier-1/Tier-2 (`0x0`/`0x80000000`) distinction, never the AX66 alias (`0x800000000`). This is a clean, well-evidenced, ax66-only gap in the syscall bridge's memory-access path.

One thing I did **not** verify and want to flag rather than guess at: I cannot, from static reading alone, prove the exact byte-for-byte mechanism connecting this out-of-bounds host pointer access to the specific reported symptom (`target socket not found for address 0x6300050980` + `mcause=0x2, mepc=0x10`). An out-of-bounds C++ read/write at a ~32 GiB-magnitude offset is undefined behavior that can plausibly corrupt unrelated host-process memory and produce exactly this kind of downstream, seemingly-nonsensical bus-level chaos - and it plausibly explains the observed asymmetry too (`handle_gettimeofday` touches one guest pointer via `guest_va_to_host`; `handle_write`/`handle_read` additionally copy a guest-supplied *length* of bytes starting from a wild pointer, which is far likelier to cross into unmapped memory than a single small fixed-size struct write) - but confirming that exact chain would need a live run under ASan/gdb, not just source reading. I'm reporting the gap itself as confirmed and the specific crash-signature explanation as a plausible, unconfirmed inference, per your ask not to fabricate certainty where the evidence doesn't reach.

Root cause found and confirmed with hard evidence (not a guess this time).

**The problem:** `ax66_makatau` stores its program's data (including the "mailbox" struct) at a special, very large address - like an alternate street address that still points to the same physical building. This is unique to `ax66`; the other two chips use plain address 0.

The "helper" code that reads the mailbox from outside was never taught about this alternate address. It only knows how to read the plain/normal address style. So when `ax66`'s program says "my mailbox is over there" using its special address, the helper's math lands completely outside the real memory.

**Confirmed in git history:** this alternate-address feature was added later, specifically for `ax66`. The commit message literally says "useful for ax66" and "other CPU doesn't touch that alias region, so no worry for other CPU" - but the person who added it never updated the mailbox-reading code to match. It's an acknowledged gap that was never finished.

**Exact locations (both need the fix, in the `vsim_andesim` repo - NOT `vplat_syscalls.c`):**
- `src/platform/sim_control.hpp` - function `dispatch()`, lines 218-225
- `src/htif/sys_call.hpp` - function `guest_va_to_host()`, lines 30-35

Both do the same wrong math: `guest_address - normal_base_address`. Neither one checks "is this guest address actually using the alternate address range instead?"

**Important correction:** your instruction was "go fix `vplat_syscalls.c`" - but that file is innocent. It's in the wrong repo (`andesim`). The real bug is in `vsim_andesim`, a different repo, in the two files above.

**One part still unproven** (the agent flagged this honestly, not confirmed): why file read/write crashes hard while just getting the time fails "cleanly." Best explanation: getting the time only touches one small piece of memory (wrong address, but survives), while file read/write copies a longer chunk of data, wandering further into memory that isn't there at all (crash). This makes sense but isn't proven without deeper debugging.

Want me to start a TDD fix in `vsim_andesim` for these two files? That repo is new to us - I'd need to learn its test setup first before writing a failing test.

content.text:
**Why ax66 fails: one piece of code uses the wrong math to find memory, only for ax66.**

Here's the simple version, with numbers.

Think of memory as a long street of numbered boxes: box 0, box 1, box 2, ... up to billions.

- **ax45 and ax46**: the program's data sits starting near box 0. Say its data is at box `5000`.
- **ax66**: the program's data sits in the SAME kind of real boxes, but ax66 calls its starting point a different, huge number instead of 0. So the same data that would be "box 5000" elsewhere is called box `34,359,743,000` by ax66. (Same real box, just a different name/number for it - like a corner building having two different door numbers, one for each street.)

Now, when the program needs outside help (check the time, read a file), it tells the helper: "my data is at box number X" - using its OWN number.

- ax45/ax46 say "box 5000." The helper does: `5000 - 0 = 5000`. Correct box. Works.
- ax66 says "box 34,359,743,000." The helper does the SAME math: `34,359,743,000 - 0 = 34,359,743,000`. But that's wrong - it should have subtracted ax66's real starting point first, not 0. So the helper goes looking at box 34,359,743,000 - a box that doesn't exist. Crash / garbage.

**Why does this happen only to ax66?** Because ax66 is the only one of the 3 chips that uses this "different big starting number" trick at all. The other two really do start near 0, so the wrong math still happens to give the right answer for them, by luck.

**Why wasn't this fixed already?** Someone added the "different big starting number" feature for ax66 back in January, but never updated the helper code to match. It's a leftover gap, not a new bug.

input.description: Check what base address main_memory's region actually uses

content.text:
**The real problem: ax66's guest memory starts at real address `0x800000000`. The code that translates guest addresses to host memory always assumes it starts at `0x0`. So for ax66, every translation is off by `0x800000000` (32 GB), landing outside the real memory buffer.**

Real facts, verified by reading the actual files just now:

**1. Where each engine's guest data actually sits (real addresses):**
```
external/ax66/andes_vip/patterns/samples/include/platform.h:37:
  #define DDR3_MEM_BASE 0x800000000

external/ax45mpv_premium/.../platform.h:36:
  #define DDR3_MEM_BASE 0x0

external/ax46mpv_advanced/.../platform.h:29:
  #define DDR3_MEM_BASE 0x0
```
`DDR3_MEM_BASE` is where the guest program's stack, heap, and global variables (including our `magicmem[8]` array) get placed. ax66 places them near `0x800000000`. The other two place them near `0x0`.

**2. The code that reads the mailbox (`sim_control.hpp:221`):**
```cpp
auto addr_offset = cmd.payload() - data_region.region.base_address;
```
- `cmd.payload()` = the guest's real magicmem address. For ax66, this is a number near `0x800000000`.
- `data_region.region.base_address` = always `0x0`. Confirmed in `platform.hpp:70`: `MemoryRegion ram_region = {RAM_BASE, RAM_END}`, and `memory_map.h:8`: `#define RAM_BASE 0x0`.
- So for ax66: `addr_offset = 0x800000000-ish - 0x0 = 0x800000000-ish`. No correction happens.

**3. What that offset gets used for (`sim_control.hpp:222`):**
```cpp
auto src = data_region.data.begin() + addr_offset;
```
`data_region.data` is the host's real memory buffer - only about 2.3 GB, sized for addresses `0x0` to `0x8FFFFFFF` (`RAM_BASE`/`RAM_END`). Adding an offset of `~0x800000000` (32 GB) walks far past the end of that buffer. That's an out-of-bounds read/write in the simulator's own program - undefined behavior. That's the crash.

**4. The exact same math, same bug, in `sys_call.hpp:33`:**
```cpp
const uint64_t off = va - data_region.region.base_address;
```
Used by every file syscall (open, read, write...) to turn a guest pointer (filename, buffer) into a real host address. Same `0x800000000` error every time.

That's it - one subtraction, using the wrong number, only wrong for ax66 because only ax66 places its data at `0x800000000` instead of `0x0`.

11	/**
12	 * A memory region in the range of `[base_address, end_address)`.
13	 * The constructor takes an inclusive end address and stores it as exclusive.
14	 * e.g. memory_region(0x80000000, 0x8fffffff) stores base=0x80000000,
15	 *      end=0x90000000.
16	 */
17	struct MemoryRegion
18	{
19	  using addr_type = uint64_t;
20	
21	  const addr_type base_address; // inclusive
22	  const addr_type end_address; // exclusive (stored as param + 1)
23	
24	  /**
25	   * @param base_address The base address of the memory region (inclusive).
26	   * @param end_address The end address of the memory region (inclusive).
27	   * @throws std::invalid_argument if base_address > end_address.
28	   * @example memory_region(0x00, 0xff) represents [0x00, 0x100)
29	   */
30	  MemoryRegion(const addr_type base_address, const addr_type end_address)
31	      : base_address{base_address}, end_address{end_address + 1}
32	  {
33	    if (base_address > end_address)
34	      throw std::invalid_argument(std::format(
35	        "invalid memory region: [{:#x}-{:#x}]", base_address, end_address));
36	  }
37	
38	  auto contains(const addr_type addr) const noexcept -> bool
39	  {
40	    return addr >= this->base_address && addr < this->end_address;
41	  }
42	
43	  auto contains(const MemoryRegion& other) const noexcept -> bool
44	  {
45	    return other.base_address >= this->base_address
46	        && other.end_address <= this->end_address;
47	  }
48	
49	  // Does this region fully contain the half-open access [addr, addr + len)?
50	  // Takes a raw access (exclusive length) rather than a MemoryRegion, so it
51	  // does NOT go through the inclusive-end ctor (which adds 1). An access whose
52	  // exclusive end lands exactly on end_address is contained, so the final byte
53	  // of the region is reachable. contains(addr) also guarantees addr <
54	  // end_address, so end_address - addr cannot underflow, and comparing len
55	  // against it avoids overflowing addr + len at the top of the address space.
56	  auto contains_access(const addr_type addr,
57	                       const addr_type len) const noexcept -> bool
58	  {
59	    return this->contains(addr) && len <= this->end_address - addr;
60	  }
61	
62	  auto overlaps(const MemoryRegion& other) const noexcept -> bool
63	  {
64	    return this->end_address > other.base_address
65	        && this->base_address < other.end_address;
66	  }
67	};
68	
69	/**
70	 * The CPU HVM subordinate-port aperture. NDS_HVM_SIZE_KB is KILOBYTES; the
71	 * decode window must equal the memory, so the KB conversion lives here, in
72	 * one named place (a *0x1000 at the bind sites once decoded a 4x window).
73	 */
74	inline auto hvm_aperture(const MemoryRegion::addr_type base,
75	                         const MemoryRegion::addr_type size_kb) -> MemoryRegion
76	{
77	  return {base, base + size_kb * 1024 - 1};
78	}
79	
80	/**
81	 * One `--print-memmap` line. Converts the stored EXCLUSIVE end back to the
82	 * inclusive last byte and the true span here, in one place, so no dump site
83	 * re-does the arithmetic (a former dump printed the exclusive end as if
84	 * inclusive and size = span + 1). Reserved holes -- regions blocked from
85	 * binding, not routable targets -- are tagged.
86	 */
87	inline auto format_region_line(const std::string_view name,
88	                               const MemoryRegion& mr,
89	                               const bool reserved = false) -> std::string
90	{
91	  return std::format("{}: [{:#x}-{:#x}] (size: {:#x}){}", name,
92	                     mr.base_address, mr.end_address - 1,
93	                     mr.end_address - mr.base_address,
94	                     reserved ? " (reserved)" : "");
95	}

input.subject: Fix ax66_makatau HTIF alias-region bug in vsim_andesim (TDD)
input.description:
Root cause confirmed (not the old L2C theory): ax66_makatau's guest DRAM is based at 0x800000000 (an "alias" window onto the same RAM), but SimControl::dispatch() (src/platform/sim_control.hpp) and guest_va_to_host() (src/htif/sys_call.hpp) in vsim_andesim always subtracted the primary region's base (0x0), never checking alias_region. Confirmed via vendor datasheet (this mechanism isn't vendor IP) and direct source reading.

RED: wrote src/tests/platform/sim_control.test.cpp (2 cases: dispatch's magicmem pointer, guest_va_to_host's tv pointer via gettimeofday), both failed for the right reason against unmodified code.
GREEN: added SimpleMemory::base_for(addr) helper (simple_memory.hpp) picking region vs alias_region by containment; wired both broken call sites to it. Also fixed a missing #include <cstdint> in htif/command.hpp (pre-existing latent gap, blocked standalone testing). All 30 vsim_andesim unit tests pass (was 0 before my new test existed; new test now green, zero regressions).

Remaining: rebuild the real sim_ax66_makatau engine binary with the fix and re-run andesim's tests/vplat/test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh + vplat_file.elf against it to confirm the real end-to-end crash is gone (in progress, background build bpt56dugg). Then decide with user whether to commit (both repos currently have uncommitted changes; user's CLAUDE.md says never commit unless asked).

content.text:
Fixed and verified at the unit level:

**The fix**: added one small helper, `base_for(addr)`, to `SimpleMemory` (`simple_memory.hpp`) - it picks the correct starting address (normal region vs. `ax66`'s special alias region) based on which one the guest's pointer actually falls in. Both broken spots (`dispatch()` in `sim_control.hpp`, `guest_va_to_host()` in `sys_call.hpp`) now call this instead of blindly assuming address 0.

**TDD steps done:**
- RED: wrote a new test file (`sim_control.test.cpp`) reproducing both broken spots. Confirmed it failed for the right reason against the unmodified code.
- Found and fixed one unrelated blocker along the way: `htif/command.hpp` was missing `#include <cstdint>` - it only ever compiled before by accident, riding on some other file including it first. Fixed that first, separately (structural, zero behavior change).
- GREEN: applied the fix. Both new tests pass.
- Ran all 30 unit tests in the repo - all pass, nothing broken.

**Now running:** rebuilding the actual `ax66_makatau` chip simulator binary with this fix, in the background (this is the real RTL/hardware simulator, slower to build than a small unit test). Once it's done, I'll re-run the original test that first showed this bug (`gettimeofday` + file read/write on the real chip) to confirm the real crash is actually gone. I'll report back when that finishes.

content.subject: Fix ax66_makatau HTIF alias-region bug in vsim_andesim (TDD)
content.description:
Root cause confirmed (not the old L2C theory): ax66_makatau's guest DRAM is based at 0x800000000 (an "alias" window onto the same RAM), but SimControl::dispatch() (src/platform/sim_control.hpp) and guest_va_to_host() (src/htif/sys_call.hpp) in vsim_andesim always subtracted the primary region's base (0x0), never checking alias_region. Confirmed via vendor datasheet (this mechanism isn't vendor IP) and direct source reading.

RED: wrote src/tests/platform/sim_control.test.cpp (2 cases: dispatch's magicmem pointer, guest_va_to_host's tv pointer via gettimeofday), both failed for the right reason against unmodified code.
GREEN: added SimpleMemory::base_for(addr) helper (simple_memory.hpp) picking region vs alias_region by containment; wired both broken call sites to it. Also fixed a missing #include <cstdint> in htif/command.hpp (pre-existing latent gap, blocked standalone testing). All 30 vsim_andesim unit tests pass (was 0 before my new test existed; new test now green, zero regressions).

Remaining: rebuild the real sim_ax66_makatau engine binary with the fix and re-run andesim's tests/vplat/test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh + vplat_file.elf against it to confirm the real end-to-end crash is gone (in progress, background build bpt56dugg). Then decide with user whether to commit (both repos currently have uncommitted changes; user's CLAUDE.md says never commit unless asked).

content.subject: Fix ax66_makatau HTIF alias-region bug in vsim_andesim (TDD)
content.description:
Root cause confirmed (not the old L2C theory): ax66_makatau's guest DRAM is based at 0x800000000 (an "alias" window onto the same RAM), but SimControl::dispatch() (src/platform/sim_control.hpp) and guest_va_to_host() (src/htif/sys_call.hpp) in vsim_andesim always subtracted the primary region's base (0x0), never checking alias_region. Confirmed via vendor datasheet (this mechanism isn't vendor IP) and direct source reading.

RED: wrote src/tests/platform/sim_control.test.cpp (2 cases: dispatch's magicmem pointer, guest_va_to_host's tv pointer via gettimeofday), both failed for the right reason against unmodified code.
GREEN: added SimpleMemory::base_for(addr) helper (simple_memory.hpp) picking region vs alias_region by containment; wired both broken call sites to it. Also fixed a missing #include <cstdint> in htif/command.hpp (pre-existing latent gap, blocked standalone testing). All 30 vsim_andesim unit tests pass (was 0 before my new test existed; new test now green, zero regressions).

Remaining: rebuild the real sim_ax66_makatau engine binary with the fix and re-run andesim's tests/vplat/test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh + vplat_file.elf against it to confirm the real end-to-end crash is gone (in progress, background build bpt56dugg). Then decide with user whether to commit (both repos currently have uncommitted changes; user's CLAUDE.md says never commit unless asked).

content.subject: Fix ax66_makatau HTIF alias-region bug in vsim_andesim (TDD)
content.description:
Root cause confirmed (not the old L2C theory): ax66_makatau's guest DRAM is based at 0x800000000 (an "alias" window onto the same RAM), but SimControl::dispatch() (src/platform/sim_control.hpp) and guest_va_to_host() (src/htif/sys_call.hpp) in vsim_andesim always subtracted the primary region's base (0x0), never checking alias_region. Confirmed via vendor datasheet (this mechanism isn't vendor IP) and direct source reading.

RED: wrote src/tests/platform/sim_control.test.cpp (2 cases: dispatch's magicmem pointer, guest_va_to_host's tv pointer via gettimeofday), both failed for the right reason against unmodified code.
GREEN: added SimpleMemory::base_for(addr) helper (simple_memory.hpp) picking region vs alias_region by containment; wired both broken call sites to it. Also fixed a missing #include <cstdint> in htif/command.hpp (pre-existing latent gap, blocked standalone testing). All 30 vsim_andesim unit tests pass (was 0 before my new test existed; new test now green, zero regressions).

Remaining: rebuild the real sim_ax66_makatau engine binary with the fix and re-run andesim's tests/vplat/test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh + vplat_file.elf against it to confirm the real end-to-end crash is gone (in progress, background build bpt56dugg). Then decide with user whether to commit (both repos currently have uncommitted changes; user's CLAUDE.md says never commit unless asked).
